Coleman's primary role during his career was as a [[kick returner]], gaining 4,466 yards and scoring two [[touchdown]]s. He also added 384 yards and a touchdown returning [[Punt (gridiron football)|punts]], and caught 43 passes for 602 yards and three touchdowns. As a [[rookie]] in 1994, Coleman played in [[Super Bowl XXIX]] with the Chargers and set several [[Super Bowl]] records in the game: most kickoff returns (8), most kickoff return yards (244), and most total return yards (244, tied with [[Desmond Howard]] in [[Super Bowl XXXI]]).  Coleman had a 98-yard kickoff return for a touchdown in the game, tied for the second longest kickoff return in [[Super Bowl]] history.

Coleman began his coaching career at [[Youngstown State Penguins football|Youngstown State]] in 2010, spending his first season as the tight ends coach and the following two seasons as their wide receivers coach.<ref>https://www.kstatesports.com/sports/football/roster/coaches/andre-coleman/41</ref> He left to coach wide receivers at his alma mater of [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State]] in 2013.<ref name="K-State Sports Information">{{Cite web |url=http://kstatesports.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/022013aaa.html |title=Andre Coleman Named Wide Receivers Coach - KSTATESPORTS.COM - the Official Athletic Site of Kansas State |access-date=July 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130910002459/http://kstatesports.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/022013aaa.html |archive-date=September 10, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Coleman added pass game coordinator to his duties in the 2016 season, and was later promoted to [[offensive coordinator]] in 2018.<ref name="K-State Sports Information"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Coleman - Football Coach |url=https://www.kstatesports.com/sports/football/roster/coaches/andre-coleman/41 |access-date=March 26, 2024 |website=Kansas State University Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

Coleman joined the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] in 2019 as an offensive analyst. He was promoted to interim wide receivers coach on December 1, 2019, and officially named wide receivers coach on January 13, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Estes |first=Taylor |date=February 25, 2019 |title=Former Kansas State offensive coordinator to join Texas' staff |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas/Article/Texas-Longhorns-Andre-Coleman-joins-Tom-Herman-staff-Kansas-State-Wildcats-129475856/ |access-date=February 25, 2019 |website=Horns247}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Coleman named wide receivers coach at Texas |url=https://texassports.com/news/2020/1/13/football-coleman-named-wide-receivers-coach-at-texas.aspx |access-date=March 26, 2024 |website=University of Texas Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He was fired after the 2021 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Galatzan |first=Matt |date=December 20, 2021 |title=Texas Parts Ways With WR Coach Andre Coleman |url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/football/longhorns-part-ways-wr-coach-andre-coleman |access-date=March 26, 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> After two years away from coaching, Coleman was hired by the [[Washington Commanders]] as an offensive assistant in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Commanders finalize coaching staff, former Hickory star Coleman named offensive assistant |url=https://www.sharonherald.com/sports/commanders-finalize-coaching-staff-former-hickory-star-coleman-named-offensive-assistant/article_e3d57d96-cc66-11ee-928c-dba36c5bee61.html |website=[[The Herald (Sharon)|The Herald]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 17, 2024}}</ref> He was promoted to assistant wide receivers and returners coach in February 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-announce-coaching-staff-promotions-title-changes|work=Commanders.com|title=Commanders announce coaching staff promotions, title changes|date=February 10, 2026}}</ref>

'''Andre Pierre Collins''' (born May 4, 1968) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He started in [[Super Bowl XXVI]] for the [[Washington Redskins]].  Collins currently serves as director of retired players for the [[National Football League Players Association]] (NFLPA), where he works to ensure retirees make successful post-football transitions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Collins - Transition Player |url=http://www.nflplayers.com/news/news_release.aspx?id=2457 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929103207/http://www.nflplayers.com/news/news_release.aspx?id=2457 |archive-date=September 29, 2007 |access-date=April 10, 2007 |website=NFL Players}}</ref>

A standout inside linebacker playing [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], Collins was named a 1989 [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] and a [[Dick Butkus Award|Butkus Award]] finalist. '''Andre Coleman''' (born July 26, 1984) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] a player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Albany Great Danes football|Albany Great Danes]] and  was signed by the NFL's [[San Diego Chargers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2007. Coleman is now a coach at Serra High School (San Diego, CA).

==Early life==
Coleman attended [[Burgard Vocational High School]] in Buffalo, New York and was a [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[High school football|football]], [[baseball]], and [[bowling]]. In football, he was an All-[[Western New York]] selection and a Class C All-State second-team selection. He shattered school record with 18 sacks and totaled 88 tackles, five forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries as a senior captain. He also played tight end and fullback andught two touchdown passes and scored three 2-point conversions.

==College career==
As a senior, he earned First-team Mid-Major All-America honors as senior. He finished career with 110 tackles, 14 sacks and 35 tackles for loss he was named First-team All-Northeast Conference last season and one of two defensive linemen with 30-plus tackles Has earned three varsity letters. In 2005, he was named squad's top defensive lineman in leading a unit that ranked 11th nationally in scoring against (17.6 points/ game) and tied for first on the team with 4.5 sacks and was second on team with 12.0 tackles for a loss. In 2004, he made 22 tackles, including four for losses as a junior. In 2003, he appeared in all 11 games and made 14 tackles, including 3.0 sacks, and had two pass deflections.

==Professional career==

===San Diego Chargers===
He was signed by the Chargers as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2007.

After being placed on the Chargers [[practice squad]] before week one in 2009 he was activated for the [[Monday Night Football|Monday Night]] game against the [[Oakland Raiders]] on September 14.

Coleman was later released by the Chargers to make room for veteran defensive tackle Alfonso Boone

'''Andre Fluellen''' (born March 7, 1985<ref>{{cite news | url = http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/players/8864/ | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120730133637/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/players/8864/ | url-status = dead | archive-date = July 30, 2012 | title = Andre Fluellen - Stats, Bio | publisher = SI.com | access-date = January 5, 2009}}</ref>) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]] and was selected in the third round of the [[2008 NFL draft]] by the [[Detroit Lions]].

==Early life==
A native of [[Cartersville, Georgia]], Fluellen attended [[Cartersville High School]], where he played on both the offensive and defensive lines. As a junior, he had 88 tackles, 10 sacks, six forced fumbles and scored two touchdowns. In his senior year, he added 93 tackles and 11 sacks. Regarded as a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Fluellen was ranked the No. 28 defensive tackle prospect in a class highlighted by the sole five-star [[Nate Robinson (American football)|Nate Robinson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-180 |title=Rivals.com |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |date= |access-date=2019-10-26}}</ref> After official visits to [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]], [[Florida Gators football|Florida]], [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]], and Florida State, Fluellen chose the Seminoles.

==College career==
After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his initial year at Florida State, Fluellen appeared in all 12 games of the [[2004 Florida State Seminoles football team|2004 season]]. Serving as a back-up to [[Brodrick Bunkley]], he finished the year with six tackles, including one for loss, and two pass breakups. Against both [[2004 Miami Hurricanes football team|Miami (FL)]] and [[2004 Duke Blue Devils football team|Duke]] he recorded two tackles each. In his sophomore season, Fluellen replaced [[Travis Johnson (defensive end)|Travis Johnson]] at defensive tackle. Recording 26 tackles on the year, he ranked second on the team behind Bunkley for most tackles by a defensive lineman. Fluellen also had 7.5 tackles for loss, and tied for third on the team in quarterback hurries with twelve. Season-highs in both tackles (eight) and tackles for loss (two) he recorded against [[2004 NC State Wolfpack football team|North Carolina State]].

As a junior, Fluellen faced the task of replacing Bunkley at the nose guard position, named one of the “ten toughest vacancies” in college football.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://insider.espn.com/college-football/blog?name=feldman_bruce&id=2359412&_slug_=ten-toughest-position-vacancies |first=Bruce |last=Feldman |title=Ten toughest position vacancies |work=ESPN Insider |date=March 8, 2006 }}</ref> Bunkley's original successor, junior college transfer Paul Griffin, tore the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee in the first quarter against [[2006 Troy Trojans football team|Troy]], the second game of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.centralfloridafuture.com/sports/fla-sports-wrap-noles-star-dt-out-for-season-1.1425438 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131008012538/http://www.centralfloridafuture.com/sports/fla-sports-wrap-noles-star-dt-out-for-season-1.1425438 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 8, 2013 |title='Noles star DT out for season |newspaper=Central Florida Future |date=September 12, 2006 }}</ref> Fluellen was moved to his position, and started at nose guard for the remainder of the season. He finished seventh on the team in tackles, and first among all defensive lineman, in tackles with a career-high 28 stops. Fluellen also had eight tackles for minus yardage (fourth on the team).

On the eve of his senior season, Fluellen was named one of the “ten seniors to watch in '07” by ''[[ESPN]]''.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/columns/story?columnist=schlabach_mark&id=2912812 |title=Amendola, Brinkley highlight seniors to watch in '07 |work=ESPN |date=June 22, 2007 }}</ref> He was named to several preseason All-American and All-Atlantic Coast Conference teams, but managed to start only five games, missing three entire contests due to a left elbow hyperextension. He ended the season with 21 tackles (10 solos), including two sacks, one pressure and a pair of pass deflections.

==Professional career==

===Pre-draft===
After his injury-plagued senior campaign, Fluellen's draft stock plummeted. In their pre-draft coverage, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' projected him to be a sixth-round draft choice.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2008/draft/players/5101.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080501090226/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2008/draft/players/5101.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=May 1, 2008 | work=CNN | title=SI Grade}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions (first stint)===
Fluellen was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the third round of the [[2008 NFL draft]], 87th overall, using the third round pick acquired in a trade with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In four years with the Lions, Fluellen played 51 games, recording 48 [[Tackle for loss|tackles]] and 2.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], [[Starting lineup|starting]] five times.<ref name="signed2">{{cite news |url=http://www.mlive.com/lions/index.ssf/2012/12/detroit_lions_place_corey_will.html |title=Detroit Lions place Corey Williams on IR, re-sign Andre Fluellen |last=Rogers |first=Justin |newspaper=[[mlive.com]] |date=December 11, 2012 |access-date=December 11, 2012}}</ref> He was released by the Lions on August 31, 2012 in one of their final roster cuts of the 2012 preseason.

===Miami Dolphins===
Fluellen was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] on September 19. He was to have a reserve role in place of the injured reserve player [[Tony McDaniel]]. He played two games with the Dolphins,<ref name="signed2" /> who released Fluellen on October 2, 2012 upon McDaniel's return to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Dolphins-Sign-Jabar-Gaffney-Make-Other-Roster-Moves/d651dd91-70a8-4ce5-a6d2-cd66e63de04b|title=Dolphins Sign Jabar Gaffney; Make Other Roster Moves|access-date=October 5, 2012|date=October 2, 2012|work=[[Miami Dolphins]]|author=|page=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004222231/http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Dolphins-Sign-Jabar-Gaffney-Make-Other-Roster-Moves/d651dd91-70a8-4ce5-a6d2-cd66e63de04b|archive-date=October 4, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions (second stint)===
Fluellen signed with the Lions on December 11, 2012.<ref name="signed2" /> He played in three games, starting one, and totaled six tackles.

===Chicago Bears===
On April 9, 2013, Fluellen was signed by the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/bears-sign-fluellen-moore-boggs-012224193--nfl.html|title=Bears sign Fluellen, Moore, Boggs|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=April 9, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013|archive-date=April 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130413031518/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/bears-sign-fluellen-moore-boggs-012224193--nfl.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Fluellen was released by the Bears on May 20, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|author=PlexusGroupe |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/05/20/bears-release-dt-andre-fluellen/ |title=Bears release DT Andre Fluellen – ProFootballTalk |publisher=Profootballtalk.nbcsports.com |date=2013-05-20 |access-date=2019-10-26}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions (third stint)===
On July 26, 2013, Fluellen was signed by the Lions, marking the third time in his career that he joined the team.<ref>{{cite news|first=Chris |last=McCosky |title=Lions bring back defensive tackle Andre Fluellen |url=http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20130726/SPORTS0101/307260096/Lions-bring-back-defensive-tackle-Andre-Fluellen |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130727042347/http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20130726/SPORTS0101/307260096/Lions-bring-back-defensive-tackle-Andre-Fluellen |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 27, 2013 |work=The Detroit News |date=July 26, 2013 }}</ref> On August 31, 2013, Fluellen was cut by the Lions organization in the effort to finalize the 53-man roster.<ref>{{cite news|title=Detroit Lions finalize 53-man roster; TE Joseph Fauria, WR Kris Durham make the team|work=[[mlive.com]]|url=http://www.mlive.com/lions/index.ssf/2013/08/detroit_lions_finalize_53-man.html|date=August 31, 2013}}</ref> In September, he was re-signed by the Lions.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/article/20130923/SPORTS01/309230102/detroit-lions-andre-fluellen |title=Detroit Lions sign DT Andre Fluellen for third time in 13 months |newspaper=Detroit Free-Press |date=September 23, 2013 }}</ref> In 8 games in 2014, he totaled 10 tackles and a career-high 2.0 sacks.

===Buffalo Bills===
On June 16, 2015, Fluellen signed a contract with the [[Buffalo Bills]]. For final roster cuts, he was released on September 4, 2015, but re-signed with the team on September 7<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-add-Andre-Fluellen-to-53-man-roster-Five-added-to-practice-squad/fc39cb66-512d-405e-a716-c4960bc9b3ff|work=BuffaloBills.com|title=Bills add Andre Fluellen to 53-man roster; Five added to practice squad|date=September 7, 2015|access-date=September 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150909034550/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-add-Andre-Fluellen-to-53-man-roster-Five-added-to-practice-squad/fc39cb66-512d-405e-a716-c4960bc9b3ff|archive-date=September 9, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was cut from the team once again on September 11, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://wivb.com/2015/09/11/bills-sign-enemkpali-to-53-man-roster-amid-reports-that-he-may-be-suspended/ |title=Bills sign Enemkpali to 53-man roster amid reports that he may be suspended |access-date=September 12, 2015 |archive-date=September 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912113441/http://wivb.com/2015/09/11/bills-sign-enemkpali-to-53-man-roster-amid-reports-that-he-may-be-suspended/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was then re-signed to the active roster the following day.<ref>[http://www.buffalorumblings.com/2015/9/12/9315003/bills-add-fluellen-to-53-man-roster-again Bills add Fluellen to 53-man roster (again)]</ref>

===Detroit Lions (fourth stint)===
On October 7, 2015, Andre Fluellen was signed by the Detroit Lions after [[Tyrunn Walker]] was placed on [[injured reserve]]. it was the ninth time Fluellen had signed with the Lions.<ref name="ninth">{{cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2015/10/07/detroit-lions-andre-fluellen/73526732/ |title=Lions sign Andre Fluellen for the 9th time |last=Birkett |first=Dave |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=October 7, 2015 |access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref>  On December 9, 2015 Fluellen was released from the [[injured reserve]] list by the Lions, making him a free agent.

He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]] before signing as a free agent in 1997 by the NFL's [[Seattle Seahawks]].{{cite news|last=Farnsworth|first=Clare|title=Rivalry Renewed: Ex-Buckeyes Springs, Galloway Running Again On The Same Field|work=Seattle Post-Intelligencer|date=1997-04-26|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/archives/1997/9704270016.asp|accessdate=2010-09-01}} He was later signed to the Broncos developmental squad in 1998, before being active the entire 1999 season.{{cite web|title=Andre Cooper|publisher=Pro Football Reference|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAn00.htm|accessdate=2010-09-01}} ==Early life== Cooper attended Duncan U. Fletcher High School in [[Neptune Beach, Florida]]. While attending high school he was a member of the football and basketball teams. He was voted runner-up "Mr. Basketball" in the state of Florida as well as "Mr. Football" in class 5A.{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=L. C.|title=Cooper Learning A New Game (page 1)|work=Orlando Sentinel|date=2002-04-09|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2002/04/09/cooper-learning-a-new-game/|access-date=2010-09-01}} He was a ''[[USA Today]]'' first-team All American. ==College career== Cooper attended [[Florida State University]]. He was a contributing member of the 1993 national championship team his freshman year.{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=L. C.|title=Cooper Learning A New Game (page 2)|work=Orlando Sentinel|date=2002-04-09|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2002/04/09/cooper-learning-a-new-game/|access-date=2010-09-01}} Cooper was a First-team All Atlantic Coast Conference selection at Wide Receiver in 1995 and 1996. He was also named Most Valuable Player in the 1996 [[Orange Bowl (game)|Orange Bowl]], in which Florida State defeated the [[University of Notre Dame]].{{cite news|last=O'Brien|first=David|title=Cooper Reaches High – And Grabs Mvp Honor|work=South Florida Sun-Sentinel|date=1996-01-02|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1996-01-02/news/9601020050_1_danny-kanell-notre-dame-derrick-mayes|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120729130538/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1996-01-02/news/9601020050_1_danny-kanell-notre-dame-derrick-mayes|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 29, 2012|accessdate=2010-09-01}} Cooper was inducted into the Orange Bowl Hall of Fame in 2014. His 15 touchdowns in 1995 is a FSU single season record. ==Professional career== Cooper signed as an undrafted free agent with the Seattle Seahawks in 1997. After being released during training camp, he signed with the Denver Broncos in 1998. Cooper was a member of the Denver Broncos development squad for the entire 1998 season as the team won back to back Super Bowl titles. In 1999, Cooper was elevated to the active roster of the Denver Broncos after leading the National Football League in receptions and receiving yards in the preseason. During the regular season, Cooper caught 9 passes for 98 yards. In 2000, Cooper was released by the Denver Broncos after the 4th game of the regular season. Brown was also a member of the [[Denver Broncos]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Washington Redskins]] and [[Houston Texans]]. ==College career== Brown played four seasons for the [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State]], rushing for 2,539 yards and 22 [[touchdown]]s on 523 carries. He rushed for 767 yards and seven touchdowns (both career highs) as a senior in 2008. ==Professional career== ===New York Giants (first stint)=== Brown was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the fourth round (129th overall) of the [[2009 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He suffered a ruptured [[Achilles tendon]] during training camp on August 14, which forced him to miss his rookie season. On September 21, 2010 Brown was signed to the active roster, and [[Lance Ball]] was waived.{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/sports/ci_16135567 |work=Denver Post |title=Broncos sign RB Andre Brown, waive Lance Ball |date=September 21, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100923133155/http://www.denverpost.com/sports/ci_16135567 |archive-date=September 23, 2010 }} Brown himself was waived on October 16, 2010. In four regular season games with the Broncos, Brown played in three but only amassed statistics in one (two rushes for a total of minus one yard in a 31-17 road loss to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on October 10, 2010).{{cite web|author =Andre Brown |url=http://www.nfl.com/players/andrebrown/gamelogs?id=BRO251022 |title=Andre Brown: Game Logs at |work=Nfl.com |date=December 15, 1986 |access-date=November 26, 2012}} ===Indianapolis Colts=== Brown was claimed off waivers by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on October 18, 2010. Brown was moved to the Colts active roster on November 6, 2010, then waived on November 9, 2010. Brown did not amass any statistics in his only game with the Colts, a 26-24 road loss to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on November 7, 2010. ===Carolina Panthers=== Brown was claimed off waivers by the [[Carolina Panthers]] on November 9, 2010, and then waived on November 16, 2010. Brown did not play in his only game with the Panthers, a 31-16 road loss to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on November 14, 2010. ===Washington Redskins=== On November 24, 2010, Brown was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] and added to their active roster.{{cite news| url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/redskinsinsider/running-backs/redskins-to-add-running-back-a.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008122230/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/redskinsinsider/running-backs/redskins-to-add-running-back-a.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=October 8, 2012 | work=The Washington Post | title=Redskins to add running back Andre Brown}} He was released on July 28, 2011.{{cite web|last=Rosenthal|first=Gregg|title=Release Tracker|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2011/07/28/release-tracker/|work=[[Pro Football Talk]]|access-date=July 29, 2011}} ===New York Giants (second stint)=== On August 3, 2011, Brown re-signed with the Giants.{{Cite web |last=Garafolo |first=Mike |date=2011-08-03 |title=Giants sign running back Andre Brown |url=https://www.nj.com/giants/2011/08/giants_sign_running_back_andre.html |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=NJ.com}} He was waived on September 3, but re-signed the next day to the practice squad. On February 5, 2012, Brown and the Giants won [[Super Bowl XLVI]] against the New England Patriots. After the game Brown became known for his celebratory song, "I got a ring", he and his teammates sang on the plane ride home and at the parade the following week. '''Andre Tierre Royal''' (born December 1, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for five seasons with the [[Carolina Panthers]] and [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football |Alabama Crimson Tide]]. In the NFL, Royal had 140 career [[tackle  (football move)|tackle ]]s, 6 solo sacks, 4 forced fumbles and 2 fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/908/andre-royal|title = Andre Royal Stats}}</ref> Royal was traded to the Indianapolis Colts following several off-the-field incidents prior to the start of the season with the [[New Orleans Saints]].

== College career ==
Royal played at the [[University of Alabama]] under head coach [[Gene Stallings]]. He was part of the [[1992 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|1992-1993 national championship team]]. He later took part in the 1995 [[Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://rolltide.com/news/2006/5/3/ALL_STAR_GAMES_Players_as_Participants_ |title=ALL STAR GAMES |website=rolltide.com }}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Royal, signed a guaranteed $4.085 million contract with the Saints as a free agent after previously attaining All-Pro status with the Carolina Panthers, and was expected to start at strong-side linebacker. He was replaced in the Saints' final exhibition game by backup Keith Mitchell.

After reporting to Saints training camp 20 or 30 players including Royal, were involved in a team publicized hazing event in [[La Crosse, Wisconsin]]. Several rookies, including [[Cam Cleeland]], were hit with a pillowcase filled with coins as they had to walk through 20 to 30 players lined up on each side of a dormitory hallway.<ref>{{cite news |date=August 31, 1998 |title=Saints Trade Troubled Linebacker Royal |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-aug-31-sp-18258-story.html |access-date=September 6, 2025 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Six players were singled out and named in a lawsuit including: Royal, [[Brady Smith (American football)|Brady Smith]], Brian Jones, Isaac Davis, Troy Davis, and Keith Mitchell. Defensive line coach, Walt Corey was also named as a defendant. Royal admitted to participating in the incident but said he did not hit the rookies with any objects as the defendants were accused of doing.<ref>The Hazing Reader by HankNuwer</ref>

The Saints' settled with the injured player. The settlement covered all the players except Royal whose suit was dismissed.<ref>The Hazing Reader by HankNuwer</ref>

After being accused of faking a head injury by Coach Mike Ditka in a team meeting; Ditka and Royal engaged in a highly publicized and televised shouting match. Ditka fined Royal $50,000 which Royal appealed to the NFL. Ditka was found to have been "baiting a player" and was fined $50,000.00 instead.<ref>ESPN</ref>

In the trade with the Colts, the Saints acquired tight end [[Scott Slutzker]] from the Colts for Royal, having been short-handed at that position because of injuries, including that of No. 2 draft pick [[Cam Cleeland]].

Royal went on to star on the field for the Indianapolis Colts leading the Defense across from Offensive All-Pro, [[Peyton Manning]]. However, after playing two seasons with the Colts, Royal's NFL Career came to an end from the effects of several head injuries.<ref>NFLPA</ref>

Royal had offered to voluntarily give up the last 2 years' salary on his four-year contract with the Colts in exchange for being allowed to retire at the end of the first season with the Colts.

Despite Royal's official retirement from the NFL in 2001, several teams approached him about returning to the NFL including the [[Dallas Cowboys]], who offered Royal a 2-year deal following his retirement.

Although Andre Royal never played football before moving to Northport, Alabama during his 8th grade year in junior high school, he went on to earn a four-year college scholarship to the [[University of Alabama]] where he studied criminal justice and played on the 1992 NCAA Division I National Football Championship Team. He also had an all-pro career in the NFL, playing on the inaugural team of the Carolina Panthers and in several NFC Championship games.

Royal returned to the University of Alabama to complete and earn his college degree in 2014.

'''Andre Alexander Ramsey''' (born July 24, 1987) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] as a 7th round draft pick in 2009. He played [[college football]] at [[Ball State Cardinals football|Ball State]].

Ramsey was also a member of the [[Buffalo Bills]], [[New York Jets]], [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[Miami Dolphins]], [[Kansas City Command]], [[Carolina Panthers]], [[BC Lions]], [[Calgary Stampeders]], and [[Orlando Predators]].

==Professional career==

===Seattle Seahawks===
After going in the 7th round of the NFL draft Ramsey went on to play in 6 games that 2009 season recording 5 starts

===Buffalo Bills===
Ramsey was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Buffalo Bills]] . He remained there until being promoted to the active roster on December 11 after [[offensive tackle]] [[Demetress Bell]] was placed on [[injured reserve]].

===New York Jets===
The [[New York Jets]] signed Ramsey October 25, 2010. Ramsey went on to start 8 games that season at right and left tackle.

===Baltimore Ravens===
After trying out for the Ravens Andre went on to play in 12 games the next season with both starts at guard and tackle help his team to the AFC championship game

===Miami Dolphins===
The team signed Ramsey to their practice squad on November 30, 2011. He was on the practice roster for one game before being released.

===Kansas City Command===
Following his release from the Dolphins Ramsey signed with the [[Kansas City Command]] of the [[Arena Football League]] . The [[2012 Arena Football League season]] spanned from March 9, 2012 – July 22, 2012.

===Carolina Panthers===
Signed as a [[free-agent]] by the Panthers on August 10, 2012. Where played in 14 games at left guard having his most productive season to date until being place on season ending IR week 14 of the season

===BC Lions===
On March 26, 2013, Andre Ramsey signed with the BC Lions of the Canadian Football League. Starting all 18 games at left tackle

===Calgary Stampeders===
In June 2015, Ramsey signed with the [[Calgary Stampeders]] where he started 12 games at left tackle

===Orlando Predators===
On December 7, 2015, Ramsey was assigned to the [[Orlando Predators]]. On May 25, 2016, Ramsey was placed on recallable reassignment.

'''Andre McXavier Roberts''' (born January 9, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] and [[return specialist]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for [[The Citadel Bulldogs football|The Citadel Bulldogs]] and was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the third round of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. Roberts played for nine teams during his NFL career (the most in league history for a wide receiver or return specialist).<ref name="Kennedy">{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39395365/who-played-most-nfl-teams | title=Who has played for the most NFL teams? | publisher=[[ESPN.com]] | date=September 3, 2025 | accessdate=21 May 2026 | author=Kennedy, Alex}}</ref> In addition to the Cardinals, he played for the [[Washington Redskins]], [[Detroit Lions]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[New York Jets]], [[Buffalo Bills]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Los Angeles Chargers]], and [[Carolina Panthers]].

==Early life==
A native of [[Fairbanks, Alaska]], Roberts attended Spring Valley High School in Columbia, South Carolina, where he was a two-sport star in [[high school football|football]] and [[Track and field|track]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raynor |first=Grace |date=June 12, 2016 |title=Former Citadel All-American Andre Roberts signs with Detroit Lions |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/former-citadel-all-american-andre-roberts-signs-with-detroit-lions/article_54d62ce8-2d2e-540f-ad34-11d25dfc1761.html |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=Post and Courier |language=en}}</ref> He earned All-region and All-area honors as a senior and led the Vikings to the regional championship and state semi-finals. He earned MVP honors for his performance in the 2005 North-South All-Star game.

In addition to football, Roberts lettered in [[Track and field|track & field]] while at Spring Valley, leading his team to the state championship in 2003 and a second-place finish as a senior, the season he captured All-State recognition. He posted personal-bests of 11.2 in the [[100 metres|100-meter dash]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Region 5-4A – Boys Results (Raw) |url=https://sc.milesplit.com/meets/17273-region-5-4a/results/34059/raw |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=SCRUNNERS.COM |language=en}}</ref> 21.91 in the [[200 metres|200-meter dash]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Outback/Azalea Invitational – Boys Results (Raw) |url=https://sc.milesplit.com/meets/14817-outbackazalea-invitational/results/32352/raw |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=SCRUNNERS.COM |language=en}}</ref> and 48.60 in the [[400 metres|400-meter dash]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SCHSL State Championships – Track & Field Meet |url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/meet/25659 |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=Athletic.net |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Roberts attended [[The Citadel, The Military College of South Carolina]] from 2006 to 2009, where he played football and ran track.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts – Football |url=https://citadelsports.com/sports/football/roster/andre-roberts/818 |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=The Citadel Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He was a three-time All [[Southern Conference]] selection and two-time FCS All American who set school records for receptions in a game (14), season (95) and career (286); receiving yards in a season (1,334) and career (3,743); [[touchdown]] receptions in a game (4), season (14) and career (37); punt return yards in a season (461) and career (1,160) as well as career all-purpose yards (5,203).<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 28, 2010 |title=Roberts Named to Another All-Decade Team |url=https://citadelsports.com/news/2010/1/28/1_28_2010_2462.aspx?path=football |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=Citadel Sports |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2018 |title=Act Like A Rookie |url=https://today.citadel.edu/act-like-a-rookie/ |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=The Citadel Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

Roberts joined The Citadel outdoor track team in mid-March 2007, earning his first Penn Relays Championship watch. He made his debut at the Furman Invitational (4/07), as he finished third in the 400 meters, running 50.91. Also at Furman, he finished second in the 200 meters with a time of 23.49. He ran a collegiate-best 200-meter time of 23.05 at the Chanticleer Invitational (4/14). He ran the anchor leg of the 4x100-meter relay that clocked 41.94 at the Southern Conference Championships (4/22), garnering All-Conference honors. Also ran the anchor leg of the 4×100-meter relay team that won at the Penn Relays for the fifth consecutive time in Citadel history.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/historical/1662379 |title=Andre Roberts, Citadel, NFL Draft - CBSSports.com - NFLDraftScout.com |website=www.cbssports.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220234319/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/historical/1662379 |archive-date=December 20, 2014}}</ref> He graduated in three and a half years with a degree in accounting.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Person |first=Joseph |date=April 25, 2010 |title=Andre Roberts' NFL dream comes true |url=http://www.thestate.com/sports/college/article14383925.html |access-date=November 20, 2016 |website=thestate.com}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
Roberts was taken in the third round with the 88th overall pick by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the [[2010 NFL draft]]. The Cardinals originally obtained the pick used to select Roberts by trading [[Anquan Boldin]] to the Baltimore Ravens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=December 25, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Roberts started out his rookie season playing limited time as a punt returner.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> As the season went on, Roberts started playing more snaps and started to move into the second receiver slot. He caught his first NFL touchdown against the [[2010 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]], a 27–24 loss in OT.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at Minnesota Vikings – November 7th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201011070min.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He caught his second NFL touchdown, a 74-yard completion, on [[Christmas]] Day against the [[2010 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]], a game that was won in the last minute 27–26.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Arizona Cardinals – December 25th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201012250crd.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
[[File:Andre roberts redskins.jpg|200px|thumb|Roberts with the [[Washington Redskins]] in 2014]]

Andre Roberts agrees to deal with Redskins |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/wr-andre-roberts-agrees-to-deal-with-redskins/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com with the intention to be the Redskins' number two wide receiver, opposite of [[Pierre Garçon]], but became the number three receiver after the signing of [[DeSean Jackson]]. He also became the team's new return specialist.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Mike |date=September 4, 2014 |title=Andre Roberts to return kicks and punts for Redskins |work=WashingtonPost.com |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/09/04/andre-roberts-to-return-kicks-and-punts-for-redskins/ |access-date=October 13, 2014}}</ref>

In the Week 4, 45–14 loss against the [[2014 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], Roberts scored one of the only two Redskins' scores in the game after catching an 18-yard pass from Cousins.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Mike |date=September 26, 2014 |title=Kirk Cousins has five turnovers, Eli Manning has five TDs, and Giants top Redskins, 45–14 |work=WashingtonPost.com |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/kirk-cousins-has-five-turnovers-eli-manning-has-five-tds-and-giants-top-redskins-45-14/2014/09/26/cf6b8294-450a-11e4-b437-1a7368204804_story.html |access-date=June 20, 2015}}</ref> It was his first touchdown with the Redskins.

In Week 11 of the [[2015 Washington Redskins season|2015 season]], Roberts returned a kick 99 yards for a touchdown against the [[2015 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kring-Schreifels |first=Jake |date=November 23, 2015 |title=Andre Roberts' Return Makes No. 1 Run Of The Week |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/blog/article-1/Andre-Roberts-Return-Makes-No-1-Run-Of-The-Week/f456aab8-067c-4724-918e-33f6655f8f54 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151128042911/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/blog/article-1/Andre-Roberts-Return-Makes-No-1-Run-Of-The-Week/f456aab8-067c-4724-918e-33f6655f8f54 |archive-date=November 28, 2015 |access-date=December 29, 2015 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> On December 21, 2015, he was placed on [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]] with a knee injury, ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda |first=Stephen |date=December 21, 2015 |title=Redskins Place Andre Roberts On Injured Reserve |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Place-Andre-Roberts-On-Injured-Reserve/0cccdc9b-9fd1-4171-b235-e1ec5c7dfd8c |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222230000/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Place-Andre-Roberts-On-Injured-Reserve/0cccdc9b-9fd1-4171-b235-e1ec5c7dfd8c |archive-date=December 22, 2015 |access-date=December 29, 2015 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref>

Roberts was released by the Redskins on May 17, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=May 17, 2016 |title=Redskins release wideout Andre Roberts |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/redskins-release-wideout-andre-roberts-0ap3000000663109 |access-date=May 18, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On June 13, 2016, Roberts signed a one-year deal with the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=June 13, 2016 |title=Lions sign Andre Roberts, will visit with Anquan Boldin |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/lions-sign-andre-roberts-will-visit-with-anquan-boldin-0ap3000000668737 |access-date=June 13, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On October 2, 2016, Roberts returned a punt 85 yards for a touchdown against the [[2016 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Chicago Bears – October 2nd, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610020chi.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During a week 11 victory over the [[2016 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]], Roberts had another punt return touchdown, this time for 55 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Detroit Lions – November 20th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611200det.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Roberts also had several critical catches during the regular season, and finished the year with 14 receptions for 188 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On March 14, 2017, Roberts signed a one-year contract with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crabtree |first=Curtis |date=March 14, 2017 |title=Report: Andre Roberts signs one-year deal with Falcons |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/report-andre-roberts-signs-one-year-deal-with-falcons |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

On September 10, 2017, in his Falcons debut, Roberts was the kickoff and punt returner in the 23–17 victory over the [[2017 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]] at [[Soldier Field]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Chicago Bears – September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100chi.htm |access-date=October 2, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> He served as the Falcons' primary kick and punt returner in 2017, while only recording one catch for 12 yards on offense.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Atlanta Falcons Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/atl/2017.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On March 23, 2018, Roberts signed with the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Eric |date=March 23, 2018 |title=WR-KR Andre Roberts Joins Jets |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/WR-KR-Andre-Roberts-Joins-jets/8d9b0228-74f0-4c6e-8a42-6f2b353e5adc |access-date=November 1, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> On September 10, in the season opener against the Detroit Lions, Roberts scored his first punt return touchdown, which went for 78 yards, as a Jet.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2018 |title=Return man Andre Roberts puts 'special' in special teams |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/jets/football-jets-t42066 |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=Newsday |language=en}}</ref> In a week 15 game against the [[2018 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]] he had a touchdown reception and added 93 yards in kick returns;<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at New York Jets – December 15th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812150nyj.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> he was named to the 2018 AFC [[Pro Bowl]] squad as a return specialist.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Eric |date=December 18, 2018 |title=Andre Roberts Will Be AFC Return Specialist at the Pro Bowl |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/andre-roberts-will-be-afc-return-specialist-at-the-pro-bowl |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=New York Jets |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 16, against the [[2018 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]], he had a 99-yard kickoff return for a touchdown and a career high 215 return yards.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2018 |title=Rodgers leads Packers to wild 44-38 overtime win over Jets |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=401030870 |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> Roberts finished with career bests for both punt and kickoff returns with 324 and a league-leading 1,174 yards, respectively, in addition to adding 10 catches for 79 yards and a score on offense.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Kick & Punt Returns |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/returns.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was the first member of the Jets named to the All-Pro team since 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Costello |first=Brian |date=January 5, 2019 |title=Andre Roberts breaks Jets' first-team All-Pro drought |url=https://nypost.com/2019/01/04/andre-roberts-breaks-jets-first-team-all-pro-drought/ |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=New York Post |language=en}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
[[File:Andre Roberts.png|thumb|Roberts at the [[2020 Pro Bowl]] ]]
On March 13, 2019, Roberts signed a two-year contract with the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Bills sign Pro Bowl returner Andre Roberts |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-pro-bowl-returner-andre-roberts |access-date=November 1, 2023 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref> During the 2019 season he caught three passes and returned 53 kicks for 888 yards;<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> he was named as an alternate to the Pro Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2019/probowl.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On September 5, 2020, Roberts was released by the Bills,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Andre Roberts out as Bills drop to 53 players |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/09/05/andre-roberts-out-as-bills-drop-to-53-players/ |access-date=September 6, 2020 |website=ProFootballTalk}}</ref> but was re-signed the following day after some additional roster adjustments.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojton |first=Nick |date=September 6, 2020 |title=Jon Feliciano, Isaiah Hodgins to IR, Bills re-sign Andre Roberts, Dean Marlowe |url=https://billswire.usatoday.com/2020/09/06/buffalo-bills-jon-feliciano-isaiah-hodgins-andre-roberts-dean-marlowe/ |access-date=September 6, 2020 |website=Bills Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

During the 2020 season, Roberts caught four passes for 34 yards, returning 29 punts for 286 yards (9.9 yards per return) and 32 kick returns for 961 yards (league-leading 30.0 yards per return).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Roberts led the AFC in total return yards and was named a Pro Bowler and Second-team All-Pro.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2020/probowl.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2020/allpro.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Kick & Punt Returns |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2020/returns.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On March 24, 2021, Roberts signed a two-year deal with the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=March 15, 2021 |title=Texans signing kick returner Andre Roberts to two-year deal |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/texans/article/Texans-to-sign-Andre-Roberts-kick-returner-16027287.php |access-date=March 15, 2021 |website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 24, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (3-24-2021) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-24-2021 |access-date=March 24, 2021 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> On October 18, 2021, Roberts was released by the Texans.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (10-19-2021) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-10-19-2021 |access-date=November 1, 2023 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On October 21, 2021, Roberts signed with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Andre Roberts|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-sign-andre-roberts|website=Chargers.com|date=October 21, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021|archive-date=October 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023233628/https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-sign-andre-roberts|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the 2021 season, he appeared in 16 games over the course of the season with two teams. He mainly had a special teams role.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He led the league in total kickoff return yards with 1,010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 NFL Kick & Punt Returns |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2021/returns.htm |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On May 2, 2022, Roberts signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=May 2, 2022 |title=Panthers bring in return specialist Andre Roberts |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/andre-roberts-return-specialist-agreed-to-terms-citadel-south-carolina |access-date=November 1, 2023 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 13, 2022, with a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=September 13, 2022 |title=Panthers place Andre Roberts on injured reserve |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/panthers-place-andre-roberts-on-injured-reserve |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He was activated on December 31.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Callihan |first=Schuyler |date=December 31, 2022 |title=Panthers Activate Josh Norman & Andre Roberts |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/panthers/news/panthers-activate-josh-norman-andre-roberts |access-date=November 2, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He played in three games in the 2022 season, playing only on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Roberts 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAn00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] at [[Weber State Wildcats football|Weber State Wildcats]] and [[Saint Mary's Gaels football|Saint Mary's Gaels]]. ==College career== Hardy played [[college football]] at [[Saint Mary's College of California]] and [[Weber State University]].{{cite news |title=Seattle signs Hardy |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=1vEuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=xzQDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3300,2058060 |newspaper=Rome News-Tribune |date=October 10, 1985 |accessdate=2010-05-09}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia Eagles=== Hardy was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the fifth round (116th overall) of the [[1984 NFL draft]]. He was released on September 4, 1985, after the Eagles acquired [[Earnest Jackson]] from the [[San Diego Chargers]]. ===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)=== On October 9, 1985, Hardy was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He was released on November 6 after playing in three games for the Seahawks.{{cite news |title=All Seahawk regulars still out |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=BecPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=XI8DAAAAIBAJ&pg=4566,936514 |newspaper=Ellensburg Daily Record |date=October 8, 1987 |accessdate=2010-05-09}} ===San Francisco 49ers=== '''Andre Neblett''' (born June 7, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] for four seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Temple Owls football|Temple Owls]] and was signed by the [[Carolina Panthers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2010. He was also a member of the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and [[New England Patriots]].

In 2016, Neblett became involved with [[NASCAR]], after he was selected as part of a national combine for the Drive for Diversity crew development program.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://owlsports.com/news/2016/5/29/football-former-owl-andre-neblett-finds-career-in-racing|title=Former Owl Andre Neblett Finds Career in Racing|publisher=Temple Owls Sports|date=May 29, 2016|access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref>

==Early life==
Raised in [[Rahway, New Jersey]], Neblett played prep football as a [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] and [[linebacker]] at [[Rahway High School]].<ref>[https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NeblAn00.htm Andre Neblett Stats], [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]. Accessed February 9, 2022. "High School: Rahway (NJ)"</ref>

==College career==
Neblett played college football at Temple, where he started in 45 games for the Owls. He earned All-Mid-American Conference honors during his career.

==Professional career==

===Carolina Panthers===
On April 30, 2010, Neblett was signed by the [[Carolina Panthers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the [[2010 NFL draft]]. On July 18, 2012, Neblett was informed by the NFL that he would be suspended for the first four games of the season for testing positive for [[performance-enhancing drugs]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.catscratchreader.com/2012/7/18/3168089/panthers-dealt-a-blow-as-dt-neblett-suspended-for-peds|title = Panthers Dealt a Blow as DT Neblett Suspended for PEDs| date=July 18, 2012 }}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
Neblett signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on May 6, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/Tryout-Players-Earn-a-Shot-at-Training-Camp/d19164fa-ee09-4608-82a7-fad920f452f4|title=Tryout Players Earn a Shot at Training Camp|accessdate=May 6, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130508232007/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/Tryout-Players-Earn-a-Shot-at-Training-Camp/d19164fa-ee09-4608-82a7-fad920f452f4|archive-date=May 8, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On August 31, 2013, Neblett was released during the final roster cuts of the preseason.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/82926/tampa-bay-buccaneers-cut-down-analysis|title = Tampa Bay Buccaneers cut-down analysis| date=August 31, 2013 }}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
Neblett signed with the [[New England Patriots]] on October 9, 2013, but was released later that week on October 12. He was re-signed when the Patriots put linebacker [[Jerod Mayo]] on injured reserve on October 16. Neblett was released again on October 21.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.patriots.com/news/2013/10/21/patriots-release-dt-andre-neblett|title = Patriots release DT Andre Neblett|access-date = October 10, 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171011073749/http://www.patriots.com/news/2013/10/21/patriots-release-dt-andre-neblett|archive-date = October 11, 2017|url-status = dead|df = mdy-all}}</ref>

'''Andre DeAngelo Ellington''' (born February 3, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the sixth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Ellington attended [[Berkeley High School (Moncks Corner, South Carolina)|Berkeley High School]], where he played [[high school football]] for the Stags football team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bilodeau |first=Kevin |date=June 11, 2016 |title=Andre, Bruce Ellington hold camp at Berkeley HS |url=http://www.live5news.com/story/32199622/andre-bruce-ellington-hold-camp-at-berkeley-hs |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=Live 5 News |language=en}}</ref> As a senior, he rushed for 1,822 yards and 24 touchdowns, and also added four other touchdowns (two receiving, two kickoff return). He accumulated 2,519 all-purpose yards as a senior. [[ESPN]] named him the #44 overall prospect and #6 running back.

Ellington also ran [[track and field]] for the [[Berkeley High School (Moncks Corner, South Carolina)|Berkeley High School]] track team. He ran a personal-best time of 10.97 seconds in the [[100 meters]] at the 2006 Taco Belt Classic Melt. He also recorded a time of 23.13 seconds in the [[200 meters]]. He was also a member of the [[4 x 100 metres relay|4 × 100 m]] (42.94 s) relay squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington – Feed |url=https://sc.milesplit.com/athletes/30019-andre-ellington/feed |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=SCRUNNERS.COM |language=en}}</ref>

He picked Clemson over scholarship offers from [[University of Florida|Florida]], [[University of Georgia|Georgia]], [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[University of Maryland|Maryland]], [[University of North Carolina|North Carolina]], [[University of South Carolina|South Carolina]], and [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]].<ref name="Clemson">{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington Profile |url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/ellington_andre00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503102324/http://www.clemsontigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/ellington_andre00.html |archive-date=May 3, 2012 |access-date=July 22, 2023 |website=Clemson Tigers Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington, 2008 All Purpose Back, Clemson |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/andre-ellington-31547?view=pv |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Andre Ellington 2011.jpg|thumb|Andre Ellington catching a ball at Clemson]]

===Freshman season===
After [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his true freshman season in 2008, Ellington had 546 total yards on 79 touches in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-ellington-1/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He rushed for 72 yards on nine carries against [[2009 Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders football team|Middle Tennessee]].<ref name="Clemson" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Middle Tennessee State at Clemson Box Score, September 5, 2009 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2009-09-05-clemson.html |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
As a sophomore in 2010, Ellington was named second-team All-ACC by [[Rivals.com]]. He rushed for 686 yards on 118 carries and 10 [[touchdown]]s. He caught 12 passes for 109 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-ellington-1/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Ellington had 140 yards in 22 carries and four catches for 48 yards against eventual national champion [[2010 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]].<ref name="Clemson" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Clemson at Auburn Box Score, September 18, 2010 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-09-18-auburn.html |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Junior season===
As a junior in 2011, Ellington rushed for 1,178 yards on 223 attempts scoring 11 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlantic Coast Conference Stats 2011 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/stats |access-date=September 29, 2012 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>  Additionally, he caught 22 passes for 109 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-ellington-1/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He earned second-team all-conference honors in recognition of his successful season.

In the [[2011 ACC Championship Game]], he ran for 125 yards and one touchdown on 20 carries, as the Tigers beat the [[2011 Virginia Tech Hokies football team|Virginia Tech Hokies]], 38–10.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2011 |title=Clemson rips No. 5 Virginia Tech to win ACC championship |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=313370228 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918160658/http://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=313370228 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 18, 2018 |access-date=November 11, 2013 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Clemson lost the [[2012 Orange Bowl]] to the [[2011 West Virginia Mountaineers football team|West Virginia Mountaineers]], by a 70–33 scoreline. Ellington rushed for 116 yards from 10 carries, including a 68-yard run for the game's opening touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 4, 2012 |title=West Virginia routs Clemson in record-setting Orange Bowl |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=320040228 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308232523/http://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=320040228 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 8, 2018 |access-date=November 11, 2013 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===Senior season===
In his final season as a senior in 2012, Ellington rushed for 1,081 yards on 212 attempts (5.1 avg) while scoring eight touchdowns. He also caught 14 passes for 232 yards and a touchdown. He earned first-team all-conference honors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-ellington-1/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished his college career at fourth on Clemson's list of all-time rushers with 3,436 yards, just below former teammate [[C. J. Spiller]], and finished third in rushing touchdowns with 33.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Clemson Tigers Rushing |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/clemson/rushing.html |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Ellington graduated from Clemson in December 2012 with a [[bachelor's degree]] in parks, recreation, and tourism management.<ref name="clemson">{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2013 |title=Graduation, Thursday, December 20, 2012, Littlejohn Coliseum |url=http://www.registrar.clemson.edu/pdf/gradDec2012.pdf |access-date=November 23, 2017 |website=Clemson.edu}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===

Ellington ran a 4.61 40-yard dash at the [[NFL Scouting Combine]], considerably slower than many anticipated, as he had multiple runs of over twenty yards during his final year at Clemson.<ref name="Clemson" />

===Arizona Cardinals===
After being projected as a second or third round pick, he slid to the third day of the draft. He was selected in the sixth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]] with the 187th overall pick by the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He scored his first career touchdown on a pass reception from [[Carson Palmer]] in Week 2 of the 2013 season against the [[2013 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Arizona Cardinals – September 15th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201309150crd.htm |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 8 of the 2013 season, Ellington rushed for 154 yards against the [[2013 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]], the highest rushing total of the week.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Arizona Cardinals – October 27th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201310270crd.htm |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Week 8 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/week_8.htm |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with 652 rushing yards on 118 attempts (5.5 avg) and three touchdowns, and also caught 39 passes for 371 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/ElliAn00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Ellington was placed on season ending injured reserve after Week 14 of 2014, having injured his hip.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weinfuss |first=Josh |date=December 8, 2014 |title=Cardinals place RB Ellington (hernia) on IR |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/11996675/andre-ellington-placed-injured-reserve-arizona-cardinals-hernia-surgery |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He recorded 201 carries for 660 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns while averaging only 3.3 yards per carry. In addition, he had 46 receptions for 395 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/ElliAn00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

After the additions of running backs [[Chris Johnson (running back)|Chris Johnson]] and [[David Johnson (running back)|David Johnson]], Ellington's role in the Arizona offense was severely reduced in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Arizona Cardinals Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/crd/2015.htm |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He did make good use of his time on the field by recording 289 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 45 carries to average an astonishing 6.4 yards per carry. In Week 10 against the [[2015 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], Ellington rushed for the 48-yard game-winning touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks – November 15th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511150sea.htm |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, in the 2015 season, Ellington finished with 	45 carries for 289 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns to go along with 15 receptions for 148 receiving yards in ten games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/ElliAn00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2016, Ellington was the Cardinals third running back behind David Johnson and Chris Johnson to start the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Arizona Cardinals Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/crd/2016.htm |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was moved up to the number two back after Chris Johnson suffered a season-ending groin injury in Week 4. Ellington ended the 2016 season playing in all 16 games rushing for 96 yards and recording 12 catches for 85 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/ElliAn00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2017, Ellington signed a one-year contract extension with the Cardinals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban, Darren |date=March 13, 2017 |title=Andre Ellington Returns To Cardinals |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Andre-Ellington-Returns-To-Cardinals/b3478caf-d559-4504-bed4-2dcf8b4a011f |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201030858/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Andre-Ellington-Returns-To-Cardinals/b3478caf-d559-4504-bed4-2dcf8b4a011f |archive-date=December 1, 2017 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> On March 29, 2017, Cardinals head coach [[Bruce Arians]] announced that Ellington would be changing his position to [[wide receiver]] for the 2017 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=March 29, 2017 |title=Andre Ellington moving from RB to WR for Cardinals |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/andre-ellington-moving-from-rb-to-wr-for-cardinals-0ap3000000796062 |access-date=March 29, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On November 20, 2017, Ellington was waived by the Cardinals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knoblauch |first=Austin |date=November 20, 2017 |title=Arizona Cardinals cut veteran RB Andre Ellington |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/arizona-cardinals-cut-veteran-rb-andre-ellington-0ap3000000880346 |access-date=November 20, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On November 21, 2017, Ellington was claimed off waivers by the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 22, 2017 |title=TRANSACTIONS: Texans claim RB Andre Ellington |url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-claim-RB-Andre-Ellington/ee6dd742-157e-4885-a959-82b9ffeae8cf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180124185527/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-claim-RB-Andre-Ellington/ee6dd742-157e-4885-a959-82b9ffeae8cf |archive-date=January 24, 2018 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> Ellington ended the 2017 season with a cumulative 20 carries for 55 yards and a touchdown along with 39 receptions for 369 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Ellington 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/ElliAn00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On February 19, 2019, Ellington signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kanno |first=Jason |date=February 19, 2019 |title=Bucs sign RB Andre Ellington |url=https://bucswire.usatoday.com/2019/02/19/bucs-sign-rb-andre-ellington/ |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=Bucs Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> On August 31, 2019, Ellington was released by the Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Spence, Santos Among Final Cuts to Get Bucs' Roster to 53 |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/spence-santos-final-cuts-bucs-53-man-roster-2019 |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

'''Andre Holmes''' (born June 16, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Hillsdale Chargers football|Hillsdale Chargers]] from 2007 to 2010 and holds the school's all-time record for receiving yardage.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 8, 2010 |title=Good to be home, Holmes sets record as Chargers win |work=The Hillsdale Daily News}}</ref> Holmes was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2011 and has also played for the [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Oakland Raiders]], [[Buffalo Bills]], and [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life==
Holmes attended [[James B. Conant High School]], where he started at [[wide receiver]] for only one season. His football coaches were Dave Pendergast and Bill Modelski. Holmes also participated in basketball, where he was coached by Tom McCormack and Jeff Stewart.

In [[track and field]], Holmes set PR of 6.85 meters in the [[long jump]] and 14.06 meters in [[triple jump]]. He was also a member of the [[4 × 200 metres relay|4 × 200m relay]] (1:29.66).

==College career==
Holmes accepted a football scholarship from [[NCAA Division II]] [[Hillsdale College]], where he was coached by Keith Otterbein.

As a sophomore, Holmes became a starter at [[wide receiver]].

As a junior, Holmes started all 12 games, posting 77 receptions for 1,076 yards.

As a senior, Holmes set single-season school records with 104 receptions for 1,368 yards and 11 touchdowns. He set a single-game school record in the team's first-round playoff game against [[St. Cloud State University]] with 16 receptions for 208 yards and two touchdowns.

Holmes finished his college career as the school's All-time receiver with 219 receptions for 3,092 yards. Holmes was twice named [[GLIAC|ALL-GLIAC]] and a [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[All-American]] honorable-mention. He was also invited to play in the [[Texas vs. The Nation]] college football all-star game.<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 9, 2010 |title=Holmes headed to All-Star game, WR accepts bid to Texas vs. The Nation game |work=The Hillsdale Daily News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pryson |first=Mike |date=December 9, 2010 |title=Hillsdale College wide receiver Andre Holmes to take part in Texas vs. The Nation All-Star Game |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/jackson/2010/12/hillsdale_college_wide_receive.html |access-date=June 6, 2020 |work=The Jackson Citizen Patriot}}</ref>

Holmes was also a member of the [[track and field]] team, winning the [[GLIAC]] title in the outdoor [[triple jump]] at the conference championships in 2006.
