===Minnesota Vikings===
Holmes was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on July 27, 2011, due to his small school background. Holmes was waived on August 29.

=== Dallas Cowboys ===
On September 5, 2011, Holmes was signed to the [[Dallas Cowboys]]' practice squad. He was promoted to the active roster on December 9, but suffered a hamstring injury and did not play in the last four games of the season.

Holmes was waived by the Cowboys on November 24, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2012 |title=Andre Holmes Released; Free Agent WR Likely To Sign |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/andre-holmes-released-free-agent-wr-likely-to-sign-332316 |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref> However, the Cowboys signed him to their practice squad three days later as a replacement to [[Danny Coale]], but Holmes was not re-signed at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |date=November 27, 2012 |title=Andre Holmes returns to practice squad |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4702120/andre-holmes-returns-to-practice-squad |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
Holmes was signed by [[New England Patriots]] on January 8, 2013, to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Vega |first=Michael |date=January 8, 2013 |title=Patriots sign WR Andre Holmes to practice squad |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/new-england-patriots/2013/01/08/patriots_sign_w_4/ |access-date=June 6, 2020 |work=The Boston Globe}}</ref> He was waived on May 10.<ref name="Source: WR Andre Holmes waived -">{{Cite web |last=Rodak |first=Mike |date=November 5, 2013 |title=Source: WR Andre Holmes waived |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4743334/source-wr-andre-holmes-waived |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[ESPN Inc.]]}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
Holmes was claimed off waivers by the [[Oakland Raiders]] on May 13, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raiders Claim Veldheer's Former Teammate, Sign 7 Tryout Players Following Rookie Camp |url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Claim-Veldheers-Former-Teammate-Sign-7-Tryout-Players-Following-Rookie-Camp/9abaec4e-2773-45d7-87e8-836e0aa4163b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912012935/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Claim-Veldheers-Former-Teammate-Sign-7-Tryout-Players-Following-Rookie-Camp/9abaec4e-2773-45d7-87e8-836e0aa4163b |archive-date=September 12, 2017 |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref> On July 27, he was suspended for the first four games of the 2013 season due to violating the league's performance-enhancing drugs policy. The Raiders activated Holmes to their roster on October 7, filling the open roster spot after the release of quarterback [[Matt Flynn (American football)|Matt Flynn]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Krause |first=Marcus |date=October 7, 2013 |title=Andre Holmes activated, Flynn's release confirmed |url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2013/10/7/4813730/wide-receiver-andrew-holmes-activated-by-oakland-raiders-takes-spot-of-released-matt |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=SB Nation}}</ref>

On January 7, 2017, Holmes caught his first career postseason touchdown from quarterback [[Connor Cook]] in the Raiders' 27–14 wildcard round loss to the [[2016 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Oakland Raiders at Houston Texans - January 7th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701070htx.htm |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
On March 18, 2017, Holmes signed a three-year, $6.5 million contract with the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=March 18, 2017 |title=WR Andre Holmes agrees to terms with Bills |url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/WR-Andre-Holmes-agrees-to-terms-with-Bills/723a842a-d3ed-4914-bba2-03489796c571 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301104142/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/WR-Andre-Holmes-agrees-to-terms-with-Bills/723a842a-d3ed-4914-bba2-03489796c571 |archive-date=March 1, 2018 |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref> On September 10, in the season-opening 21–12 victory over the [[2017 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], he recorded his first touchdown as a Bill, a one-yard pass from quarterback [[Tyrod Taylor]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Buffalo Bills - September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100buf.htm |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Holmes was placed on injured reserve on December 26, 2017, with a neck injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=December 26, 2017 |title=Bills add three to active roster from practice squad |url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-add-three-to-active-roster-from-practice-squad/607e5451-c238-4798-84ae-5c46fb4b19d0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408195157/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-add-three-to-active-roster-from-practice-squad/607e5451-c238-4798-84ae-5c46fb4b19d0 |archive-date=April 8, 2018 |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

During the 2018 season, Holmes played in over 70% of special team snaps for the Bills. On December 4, 2018, Holmes was released.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=December 4, 2018 |title=Bills release WR Kelvin Benjamin in a series of roster moves |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-make-a-series-of-roster-moves |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On December 5, 2018, Holmes was claimed off waivers by the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=December 5, 2018 |title=Broncos place Emmanuel Sanders on IR, claim WR Andre Holmes off waivers from Bills |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-place-emmanuel-sanders-on-ir-claim-wr-andre-holmes-off-waivers-from-bill |access-date=June 6, 2020 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> On December 28, he was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 28, 2018 |title=Broncos Injury Report: Phillip Lindsay, Andre Holmes placed on injured reserve |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-injury-report-phillip-lindsay-andre-holmes-placed-on-injured-reserve |access-date=December 14, 2020 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> Holmes was released on January 23, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=2019-01-23 |title=Broncos cut Andre Holmes |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/broncos-cut-andre-holmes |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Orlandus Andre Branch''' (born July 14, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]]. He was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the second round of the [[2012 NFL draft]] with the 38th overall pick.

==College career==
Branch attended [[Clemson University]] from 2007 to 2011. For his career he had 179 tackles and 17.5 sacks. As a senior in 2011, he was a first-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] pick after recording 77 tackles and 10.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112811aae.html |title=Virginia Tech and Clemson Dominate All-ACC Football Teams |access-date=January 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121209065504/http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112811aae.html |archive-date=December 9, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Branch was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the second round of the [[2012 NFL draft]] with the 38th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 29, 2012, he signed a 4-year, $5.1 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars sign Andre Branch|url=http://www.news4jax.com/sports/Jaguars-sign-Andre-Branch/-/475646/14282070/-/q07fh8z/-/index.html|work=News4Jax.com|accessdate=May 29, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531092727/http://www.news4jax.com/sports/Jaguars-sign-Andre-Branch/-/475646/14282070/-/q07fh8z/-/index.html|archive-date=May 31, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
Branch signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] in on March 17, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Sign Andre Branch|url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/press-releases/article-1/PRESS-RELEASE-Dolphins-Sign-Andre-Branch/83b31a45-5086-40c7-b730-f9c12372d46c|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=March 16, 2016|access-date=March 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160319025926/http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/press-releases/article-1/PRESS-RELEASE-Dolphins-Sign-Andre-Branch/83b31a45-5086-40c7-b730-f9c12372d46c|archive-date=March 19, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his first year in Miami, Branch started 11 of 16 games for the Dolphins, posting a career-high 49 tackles to go along with 5.5 sacks and two forced fumbles.

On March 8, 2017, Branch signed a three-year, $24 million contract extension with the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Miami Dolphins to re-sign DE Andre Branch|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/miami-dolphins-to-re-sign-de-andre-branch-0ap3000000791480|author=Patra, Kevin|website=NFL.com|date=March 8, 2017}}</ref> He started 14 games in 2017, recording 23 combined tackles and 4.5 sacks.

Following a Week 1 game in 2018, Branch was fined $10,026 for taunting [[Taylor Lewan]] after delivering a concussion to Lewan with a blind side hit.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins' Andre Branch fined by NFL for taunting after hit to Titans' Taylor Lewan|url=https://www.tennessean.com/amp/1303867002|author=Bacharach, Erik|website=Tennessean.com|date=September 14, 2018|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref>

On March 2, 2019, Branch was released by the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins to release veteran DE Andre Branch|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001020190/article/dolphins-releasing-veteran-de-andre-branch|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306045253/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001020190/article/dolphins-releasing-veteran-de-andre-branch|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2019|author=Bergman, Jeremy|website=NFL.com|date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

'''Andre Jeroy Hal Jr.''' (born May 30, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He spent his five-year NFL career with the [[Houston Texans]] who selected him in the seventh round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]].

==Early life==
Hal attended Port Allen High School in [[Port Allen, Louisiana]], where he was a senior captain and a four-year starter at [[defensive back]]. As a senior, he helped lead his team to the district title and advance to first round of 3A state playoffs. He collected 53 total tackles and four interceptions as a senior, earning first-team 3A All-State honors after returning five kickoffs for scores, and contributing with three touchdown receptions on offense. He also was a member of the school's track and field team, and was part of the 3A state champion 4x200-meter relay foursome (TJ Herbert, Mitchell Moore, Johnathan Johnson) that also set the state record, third fastest time in the nation.

Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], he was rated as the 56th best [[cornerback]] prospect of his class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Hal, 2010 Cornerback, Vanderbilt |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/andre-hal-49800?view=pv |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Hal attended [[Vanderbilt University]], where he played with the Commodores football team from 2010 to 2013. As a true freshman in 2010, he appeared in all 12 games, and started two games late into the season, finishing with 15 total tackles and also averaged 23.6 yards on 11 kickoff returns. In 2011, he recorded 21 tackles, and as kickoff returner, he averaged 23.8 yards, collecting 738 yards on 31 returns, including a 96-yard touchdown return against [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia]]. In 2012, he started all 13 games, registering 48 tackles, two interceptions and a team leading 14 passes defended. As a senior in 2013, Hal earned second-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] honors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2013 |title=Matthews, Johnson, Ladler, Hal on Coaches' All-SEC team |url=http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121013aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170105084633/http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121013aaa.html |archive-date=January 5, 2017 |access-date=May 10, 2014 |website=Vanderbilt Commodores Athletics}}</ref> He finished with 49 total tackles, including 6.5 for loss, three interceptions, a fumble recovery, and an SEC leading 18 passes defended.

===2014===
The [[Houston Texans]] selected Hal in the seventh round (216th overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was the 29th cornerback selected.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans select CB Andre Hal|url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-select-CB-Andre-Hal/08c1240c-cf76-4181-9fb5-9791d8817a7e|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901031759/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-select-CB-Andre-Hal/08c1240c-cf76-4181-9fb5-9791d8817a7e|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 1, 2017|author=Sidhu, Deepi|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=May 10, 2014|access-date=August 31, 2017}}</ref>

On May 15, 2014, the Texans signed Hal to a four-year, $2.28 million [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $69,124.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Andre Hal contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/houston-texans/andre-hal-14627/| access-date=April 5, 2018| website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, secondary coach [[John Butler (American football coach)|John Butler]] held an open competition for the job as the third cornerback on the depth chart. The competition included [[A. J. Bouye]], [[Brandon Harris]], [[Josh Victorian]], [[Elbert Mack]], and [[Marcus Williams (cornerback)|Marcus Williams]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans open backup CB competition with clean slate| url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/article/Texans-open-backup-CB-competition-with-clean-slate-5668238.php| access-date=April 5, 2018| website=houstonchronicle.com| author=Roberson, Dale| date=August 4, 2014}}</ref> Head coach [[Bill O'Brien (American football)|Bill O'Brien]] named Hal the fifth cornerback on the depth chart to start the regular season, behind [[Johnathan Joseph]], [[Kareem Jackson]], A. J. Bouye, and Elbert Mack.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Houston Texans Depth Chart: 09/01/2014| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/162/HOU| access-date=April 5, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Texans' season-opener against the [[Washington Redskins]] and made his first career tackle on returner [[Andre Roberts (American football)|Andre Roberts]] during a 28-yard kick return in the second quarter of their 17–6 victory.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 1-2014: Washington Redskins @ Houston Texans| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014090703/2014/REG1/redskins@texans| access-date=April 5, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> Prior to Week 5, the Houston Texans promoted Hal to the role as the third cornerback on the depth chart after A. J. Bouye suffered a groin injury and backup [[Darryl Morris (American football)|Darryl Morris]] sustained an ankle injury during their victory against the [[Buffalo Bills]] the previous week.<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans report: Hal to step in for injured CBs| url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-report-Hal-to-step-in-for-injured-CBs-5800209.php| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=houstonchronicle.com| author=McClain, John| date=October 3, 2014}}</ref> On November 2, 2014, Hal recorded a season-high seven combined tackles and two pass deflections during a 31–21 loss to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He was a healthy scratch for two consecutive games (Weeks 14–15). Hal finished his rookie season in {{NFL Year|2014}} with 21 combined tackles (18 solo) and four pass deflections in 14 games and 14 starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Andre Hal (career)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrehal/2543874/careerstats| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===2015===
During organized team activities and training camp, Hal started a conversion to the safety position.<ref>{{cite web| title=Changed Body, Multiple Positions for Hal| url=http://houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Changed-body-multiple-positions-for-Andre-Hal/1ec73c33-afc0-439f-aea6-38580f21c34e| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170624171546/http://houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Changed-body-multiple-positions-for-Andre-Hal/1ec73c33-afc0-439f-aea6-38580f21c34e| url-status=dead| archive-date=June 24, 2017| access-date=April 5, 2018| website=HoustonTexans.com| author=Dougherty, Drew| date=June 2, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Andre Hal settling in at safety| url=http://houston.cbslocal.com/2015/08/18/andre-hal-settling-in-at-safety/| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=houston.cbslocal.com| date=July 9, 2015}}</ref> Texans' staff chose to move him to safety after it became evident his ability to earn playing time at cornerback would be difficult due to the arrival of [[2015 NFL draft|2015]] first round pick [[Kevin Johnson (cornerback)|Kevin Johnson]] and the presence of Johnathan Joseph, Kareem Jackson, and A. J. Bouye. Throughout training camp, Hal competed against [[Eddie Pleasant]], [[Lonnie Ballentine]], and [[Stevie Brown]] for the job as the starting strong safety after it was left vacant due to the release of [[D. J. Swearinger]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans' strong safety competition still unresolved between Hal, Pleasant| url=https://blog.chron.com/ultimatetexans/2015/08/texans-strong-safety-competition-still-unresolved-between-hal-pleasant/| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=blog.chron.com| author=Wilson, Aaron| date=August 24, 2015}}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Romeo Crennel]] named Hal the backup strong safety behind newly acquired free agent [[Quintin Demps]] to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans v. Chiefs: New (Unofficial) Houston Texans Depth Chart| url=https://www.battleredblog.com/platform/2015/9/12/9309281/texans-v-chiefs-new-unofficial-houston-texans-depth-chart| access-date=April 5, 2018| website=battleredblog.com| date=September 12, 2015}}{{Dead link|date=May 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Wexler: Texans 53-man roster prediction| url=https://www.click2houston.com/sports/wexler-texans-53-man-roster-prediction| access-date=April 5, 2018| website=click2houston.com| author=Wexler, Adam| date=April 2, 2015}}</ref>

On October 18, 2015, Hal earned his first career start at strong safety in place of Quintin Demps, who sustained a [[hamstring]] injury the previous week.<ref>{{cite web| title=Wednesday Injury Report: Texans at Jaguars| url=http://houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Wednesday-Injury-Report-Texans-at-Jaguars/2d2aa73b-39f8-4540-8cd3-0e3424e51041| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151018003501/http://houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Wednesday-Injury-Report-Texans-at-Jaguars/2d2aa73b-39f8-4540-8cd3-0e3424e51041| url-status=dead| archive-date=October 18, 2015| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=houstontexans.com| date=October 14, 2015}}</ref> Hal recorded three combined tackles, two pass deflections, two interceptions, and his first career touchdown during their 31–20 victory at the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He made his first career interception in the third quarter off a pass by quarterback [[Blake Bortles]] that was intended for tight end [[Julius Thomas]]. In the fourth quarter, he intercepted Bortles for the second time and returned it for a 31-yard touchdown.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 5-2015: Houston Texans @ Jacksonville Jaguars| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2015101807/2015/REG6/texans@jaguars| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 29, 2015, head coach Bill O'Brien notified Hal that he would replace [[Rahim Moore]] as the starting free safety for the upcoming game in Week 8. He earned the role after performing well while filling in at strong safety for Quintin Demps (Weeks 6–7) during his absence. The switch was also partly due to Moore's issues with tackling and his poor pursuit angles.<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans bench free safety Rahim Moore, replace him with Andre Hal| url=https://blog.chron.com/ultimatetexans/2015/11/texans-bench-free-safety-rahim-moore-replace-him-with-andre-hal/| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=blog.chron.com| author=Wilson, Aaron| date=November 1, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Texans safety Rahim Moore mortified at being inactive| url=http://www.espn.com/blog/houston-texans/post/_/id/13803/texans-safety-rahim-moore-mortified-at-being-inactive| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=ESPN.com| author=Ganguli, Tania| date=November 2, 2015}}</ref> On November 1, 2015, he made his first start as the starting free safety and recorded two solo tackles in the Texans' 20–6 win against the [[Tennessee Titans]]. In Week 13, Hal collected a season-high five combined tackles and deflected a pass in the Texans' 30–21 loss at the Bills. On January 3, 2016, he made four combined tackles, a season-high two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by Blake Bortles in their 30–6 victory against the Jacksonville Jaguars.<ref name="stats15">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Andre Hal (2015)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrehal/2543874/gamelogs?season=2015| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2015}} season with 36 combined tackles (27 solo), a career-high ten pass deflections, a career-high four interceptions, and a touchdown in 16 games and 11 starts.<ref name="career"/> Pro Football Focus gave Hal an overall grade of 71.1 in his first season as a safety.<ref>{{cite web| title=Top 10 NFL secondaries this season| url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/pro-top-10-nfl-secondaries-this-season-2| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=profootballfocus.com| author=Rollins, Brent| date=December 31, 2015}}</ref>

The Texans finished first in the [[AFC South]] with a 9–7 record. On January 9, 2016, Hal started his first career playoff game and recorded five combined tackles during a 30–0 loss against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the AFC Wildcard Game.<ref name="stats15"/>

===2016===
Head coach Bill O'Brien retained Hal and Demps as the starting safety duo to start the 2016 regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans release unofficial depth chart for Chicago| url=http://houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-release-unofficial-depth-chart-for-Chicago/476cd394-412a-4103-a073-8fb6c52300ef| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180226212109/http://houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-release-unofficial-depth-chart-for-Chicago/476cd394-412a-4103-a073-8fb6c52300ef| url-status=dead| archive-date=February 26, 2018| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=houstontexans.com| date=September 6, 2016}}</ref>

He started the Texans' season-opener against the [[Chicago Bears]] and made two combined tackles, a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Jay Cutler]] in their 23–14 victory. On October 16, 2016, Hal recorded four combined tackles and made his first career sack on quarterback [[Andrew Luck]] during a 26–23 victory against the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. In Week 8, he collected a season-high five combined tackles in the Texans' 20–13 win against the [[Detroit Lions]]. Hal was inactive for the Texans' Week 13 loss at the [[Green Bay Packers]] due to an unspecified illness.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2016 |title=Injury report: QB Aaron Rodgers officially listed as questionable |url=https://www.packers.com/news/injury-report-qb-aaron-rodgers-officially-listed-as-questionable-18191763 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> Upon his return, he was demoted to backup free safety behind [[Corey Moore (safety)|Corey Moore]] for the remainder of the season. His demotion was due to multiple missed tackles.<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans safety Andre Hal: 'I wasn't playing how I was supposed to play'| url=https://m.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-safety-Andre-Hal-I-wasn-t-playing-how-I-11302756.php| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=chron.com| author=Wilson, Aaron| date=July 20, 2016}}</ref> Hal finished the {{NFL Year|2016}} season with 48 combined tackles (32 solo), seven pass deflections, and two interceptions in 15 games and 11 starts.<ref name="career"/> He received the 60th highest overall grade from Pro Football Focus out of the 90 qualifying safeties in 2016.

The Texans finished top of their division with a 9–7 record for the second consecutive season. Defensive coordinator Romeo Crennel opted to start Hal at starting free safety over Corey Moore for the playoffs and the Texans went on to defeat the [[Oakland Raiders]] 27–14 in the AFC Wildcard Game. On January 14, 2017, Hal recorded six combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass [[Tom Brady]] during a 34–16 loss at the [[New England Patriots]] in the AFC Divisional Round.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Andre Hal (2016)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrehal/2543874/gamelogs?season=2016| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===2017===
Hal entered training camp slated as the starting free safety and saw minimal competition from Corey Moore, [[K. J. Dillon]], and Eddie Pleasant.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beggs |first=Luke |date=July 7, 2017 |title=2017 Houston Texans Training Camp Preview: Sizing Up The Safeties |url=https://www.battleredblog.com/2017/7/15/15976100/2017-houston-texans-training-camp-preview-sizing-up-the-safeties |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=Battle Red Blog}}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Mike Vrabel]] named Hal the starting free safety to start the regular season, along with strong safety Corey Moore.<ref>{{cite web| title=Texans unofficial depth chart for preseason opener| url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-unofficial-depth-chart-for-preseason-opener/470abc81-39a7-4594-94eb-b217c6334b79| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407054157/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-unofficial-depth-chart-for-preseason-opener/470abc81-39a7-4594-94eb-b217c6334b79| url-status=dead| archive-date=April 7, 2018| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=HoustonTexans.com| date=August 4, 2017}}</ref>

On August 31, 2017, the Houston Texans signed Hal to a three-year, $15 million contract extension with $7 million guaranteed.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Andre Hal gets three years, $15 million extension|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/08/31/andre-hal-gets-three-years-15-million/|author=Williams, Charean|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=August 31, 2017}}</ref>

On October 1, 2017, Hal recorded four combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted two passes by [[Marcus Mariota]] during a 57–14 victory against the Titans. The following week, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles and broke up a pass in the Texans' 42–34 loss to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Andre Hal (2017)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrehal/2543874/gamelogs?season=2017| access-date=April 6, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2017}} season with a career-high 71 combined tackles (47 solo), five pass deflections, and three interceptions in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Hal 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HalxAn00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Houston Texans did not qualify for the playoffs after finishing with a 4–12 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Houston Texans Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/htx/2017.htm |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2018===
On June 6, 2018, it was revealed that Hal was diagnosed with [[Hodgkin's Lymphoma]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=June 8, 2018 |title=Texans' Andre Hal diagnosed with Hodgkin's Lymphoma |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-Andre-Hal-diagnosed-with-Hodgkins-Lymphoma-12979331.php?ipid=happening |access-date=June 8, 2018 |website=Chron.com}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/non-football illness list on September 1, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Transactions: Texans cut roster to 53 |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transactions-texans-cut-roster-to-53 |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> After his cancer went into remission on September 26, 2018, he was activated off the NFI list to the active roster on October 20, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ragatz |first=Will |date=September 26, 2018 |title=Texans Safety Andre Hal's Cancer in Remission |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/09/26/houston-texans-andre-hal-remission-cancer-hodgkins-lymphoma |access-date=October 21, 2018 |website=SI.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2018 |title=Transaction: Texans activate S Andre Hal off Reserve/Non-Football Illness list |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transaction-texans-activate-s-andre-hal-off-ir |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> Hal made his first start of 2018 against the Jaguars in Week 7 on October 21, 2018. He had one tackle in the 20–7 win. He finished the season with 13 tackles, five passes defended, and three interceptions through eight games and two starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Hal 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HalxAn00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On April 2, 2019, Hal announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref name="Retire">{{Cite web |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-safety-Andre-Hal-retire-not-health-related-13735707.php |title=Texans safety Andre Hal retiring, says it's not health-related |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |year=2019 |website=chron.com |access-date=April 2, 2019}}</ref>

'''Andre Elton Hardy Jr.''' (born March 18, 1987) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[tight end]].

==Early life and college basketball career==
Hardy was born in [[San Diego]]. His father, [[Andre Hardy]], was a running back who played in the NFL from 1984 to 1987. Hardy played basketball at [[St. Augustine High School (San Diego)|St. Augustine High School]] in San Diego. While an all-state and all-county player, Hardy did not earn GPA and [[SAT]] scores high enough for [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] eligibility. Thus, his family decided to have Hardy miss one credit for graduation from St. Augustine and transfer to the [[New Hampton School]].<ref name="USF loses 2 of 3 recruits">{{cite web|last1=McCulloch|first1=Will|title=USF loses 2 of 3 recruits|url=http://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/USF-loses-2-of-3-recruits-2579162.php|website=San Francisco Chronicle|accessdate=January 24, 2015|date=July 28, 2007}}</ref> Although Hardy committed to the [[University of San Francisco]] while at New Hampton, the university ultimately did not admit Hardy, so Hardy enrolled at [[Oral Roberts University]] the summer after graduating from New Hampton in 2007.<ref name="USF loses 2 of 3 recruits"/>

With the [[Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball|Oral Roberts Golden Eagles]], Hardy averaged 4.1 points and 3.6 rebounds as a freshman in 2007–08. That season, Oral Roberts won the [[2008 The Summit League men's basketball tournament|Summit League tournament]] and an automatic berth to the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]].<ref name="Cal State Fullerton bio">{{cite web|title=Andre Hardy|url=http://www.fullertontitans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hardy_andre00.html|publisher=Cal State Fullerton Titans|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120514164320/http://www.fullertontitans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hardy_andre00.html|archivedate=May 14, 2012}}</ref> Hardy then averaged and 7.5 points and 5.5 rebounds as a sophomore in 2008–09.<ref name="Hardy stats">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/andre-hardy-1.html|title=Andre Hardy College Stats|publisher=Sports-Reference|accessdate=March 30, 2022}}</ref>

He then transferred to [[Cal State Fullerton Titans men's basketball|Cal State Fullerton]] and sat out the 2009–10 season per NCAA transfer rules. Hardy missed the first 12 games of the season due to ankle surgery but led the team in rebounding with 8.5 per game, in addition to averaging 10.6 points per game.<ref name="Cal State Fullerton bio"/><ref name="Hardy stats"/> Hardy was elected [[Big West Conference|Big West]] Newcomer of the Year by conference coaches.<ref name="Cal State Fullerton bio"/> As a senior, Hardy averaged 4.9 points and 4.5 rebounds; he left the team in January 2012 for personal reasons.<ref name="Hardy stats"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/andre-hardy-1/gamelog/2012/|title=Andre Hardy 2011-12 Game Log|publisher=Sports-Reference|accessdate=March 30, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Sign Hardy|url=http://www.fullertontitans.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041312aaa.html|publisher=Cal State Fullerton Titans|accessdate=January 24, 2015|date=April 13, 2012}}</ref>

==NFL career==
Hardy signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an undrafted free agent on April 12, 2012 and was released on May 14, 2012.<ref name="Cardinals bio">{{Cite web |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/team/roster/Andre-Hardy/8c573702-9770-412d-b202-1ddafc4bd7b5 |title=Arizona Cardinals: Andre Hardy |access-date=January 25, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141229052343/http://www.azcardinals.com/team/roster/andre-hardy/8c573702-9770-412d-b202-1ddafc4bd7b5/ |archive-date=December 29, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On January 7, 2014, Hardy signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on a futures contract.<ref name="Cardinals bio"/> During the preseason, Hardy made 2 receptions for 24 yards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrehardy/2535437/gamelogs|title = NFL Players | Past & Current NFL Players|website = [[NFL.com]]|accessdate=March 30, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on the practice squad on August 31.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blog.azcardinals.com/2014/08/31/cards-claim-linebacker-keiser-cut-powell/|title=Cards claim linebacker Keiser, cut Powell|publisher=Arizona Cardinals|date=August 31, 2014|accessdate=March 30, 2022|archive-date=October 21, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021211452/http://blog.azcardinals.com/2014/08/31/cards-claim-linebacker-keiser-cut-powell/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 30, Hardy was placed on the practice squad injured reserve after a calf injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.revengeofthebirds.com/2014/12/30/7472037/arizona-cardinals-make-practice-squad-move-with-injury-to-andre-hardy|title = Cards add TE Bolser to practice squad; Hardy hurt|website=RevengeoftheBirds.com|publisher=SBNation|date = December 30, 2014|accessdate=March 30, 2022}}</ref>

'''Andre Patton''' (born May 28, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.scarletknights.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=334|title=Andre Patton - 2016 Football Roster - The Official Site of Rutgers Athletics|website=ScarletKnights.com|access-date=September 8, 2017}}</ref> and was signed by the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2017.

==Early life==
Patton was a two-way starter for the St. Elizabeth Vikings football team. On offense, his senior year he had 48 catches for 761 yards and eight touchdowns and rushed for 677 yards and 14 touchdowns. On defense, Patton recorded 68 tackles and three interceptions and was named the Delaware Defensive Player of the Year by voting media and the Delaware Interscholastic Football Coaches Association.  He was rated Delaware's top recruit Rivals.com, ESPN.com and 247Sports.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersfootball/index.ssf/2013/02/national_signing_day_2013_rutg_1.html|title=National Signing Day 2013: Rutgers football recruiting class|website=NJ.com|access-date=September 8, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
Patton saw game action in each of his four years at Rutgers. He finished his senior year with 33 receptions for 460, as well as 5 touchdown receptions, which lead the team and was good enough for ninth in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]].<ref name=":0" />

'''Andre Clyde Dillard''' (born October 3, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State Cougars]] and was drafted by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] 22nd overall in the [[2019 NFL draft]]. Dillard has also played for the [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[Green Bay Packers]].

==College career==
[[File:Andre Dillard.jpg|thumb|Dillard in 2018|left]]
After [[redshirted|redshirting]] his first year at Washington State, Dillard played only three games during his freshman season at left tackle.

Before his junior season, strength coach Marco Candido repositioned Dillard as the replacement for left tackle [[Joe Dahl]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2016/mar/26/cougars-prepare-andre-dillard-as-capable-replaceme/|title=Cougars prepare Andre Dillard as capable replacement to Joe Dahl at left tackle|author=Thorpe|first=Jacob|date=March 26, 2016|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|publisher=[[Cowles Company]]|access-date=May 3, 2018}}</ref> During his next two seasons, he started all 26 games at left tackle.

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Dillard was drafted by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] with the 22nd overall pick in the first round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/eagles-trade-up-with-ravens-to-pick-andre-dillard-0ap3000001028108|title=Eagles trade up with Ravens to pick Andre Dillard|last1=Bergman|first1=Jeremy|date=April 25, 2019|publisher=[[National Football League]]|access-date=April 26, 2019}}</ref> He played in all 16 games as a rookie, starting four in place of injured starters.

Dillard entered training camp in 2020 as the projected starting left tackle. However, on August 27, 2020, he suffered torn biceps and was ruled out for the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Andre Dillard out for season with torn biceps|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/08/27/report-andre-dillard-out-for-season-with-torn-biceps/|author=Smith, Michael David|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 27, 2020}}</ref> Dillard was placed on [[injured reserve]] on September 3.<ref>{{cite news |author=McPherson, Chris |title=Eagles place Andre Dillard on Injured Reserve; waive 12 players |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-place-andre-dillard-on-injured-reserve-waive-12-players |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=September 3, 2020 |access-date=September 4, 2020}}</ref>

Dillard entered training camp in 2021 in a battle with [[Jordan Mailata]] for the starting left tackle role, but began the season as a backup. Due to an absence by [[Lane Johnson]], Dillard started four games from Weeks 3 to 6 at left tackle with Mailata having been moved to right tackle during that time. Dillard was placed on the COVID list on December 20.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dickerson and Dillard Land on Reserve/COVID-19 List |url=https://www.sportstalkphilly.com/2021/12/dickerson-and-dillard-land-on-reservecovid-19-list.html |author=Lipinski, Michael |website=SportsTalkPhilly.com |date=December 20, 2021}}</ref> He was removed from the COVID list nine days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=Eagles activate 4 players from the Reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-activate-4-players-from-the-reserve-covid-19-list |author= McPherson, Chris |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=December 29, 2021}}</ref>

The Eagles declined the fifth-year option on Dillard's contract on May 2, 2022, making him a free agent after the season.<ref name="j996">{{cite web |title=Fifth-year option tracker for first-round picks from the 2019 NFL Draft |website=NFL.com |date=April 25, 2022 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/fifth-year-option-tracker-for-first-round-picks-from-the-2019-nfl-draft |access-date=September 7, 2024}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 6.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hurley |first=Sage |date=September 6, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Eagles place T Andre Dillard on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/roster-moves-eagles-place-andre-dillard-on-injured-reserve |access-date=November 1, 2024 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> Dillard was activated on October 15.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hurley |first=Sage |date=October 15, 2022 |title=Eagles activate Andre Dillard from Injured Reserve |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-activate-andre-dillard-from-injured-reserve |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 20, 2023, Dillard signed a three-year, $29 million contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=March 20, 2023 |title=Titans Agree to Terms With Former Eagles Tackle Andre Dillard |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-reach-deal-with-former-eagles-tackle-andre-dillard |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> He was named the starting left tackle and started 10 of 16 games played. Dillard was released on March 15, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Release Offensive Lineman Andre Dillard|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-release-offensive-lineman-andre-dillard|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=March 15, 2024}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On April 18, 2024, Dillard signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 18, 2024|title=Packers sign T Andre Dillard|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-t-andre-dillard|access-date=April 18, 2024|website=Packers.com}}</ref> He was named a backup tackle, playing almost exclusively on special teams.

===San Francisco 49ers===
On May 9, 2025, Dillard signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Sign Dillard, Flowers, Petit-Frere and 12 Rookies; Waive Three Players|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-dillard-flowers-petit-frere-and-12-rookies-waive-three-players|website=49ers.com|date=May 9, 2025|access-date=May 9, 2025}}</ref> On August 14, he was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Sign Two Defensive Lineman, Place Dillard on IR, Waive Another|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-two-defensive-lineman-place-dillard-on-ir-waive-another|website=49ers.com|date=August 14, 2025|access-date=August 14, 2025}}</ref> On August 25, Dillard was released by the 49ers with an injury settlement.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andre Dillard: Bound for free agency|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/andre-dillard-bound-for-free-agency/|work=CBS Sports|date=August 25, 2025|access-date=August 26, 2025}}</ref> On October 28, Dillard was re-signed to the 49ers' practice squad, but was released two days later.<ref>{{Cite web|title=San Francisco 49ers Sign OL Dillard to Practice Squad, Release Player|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/san-francisco-49ers-sign-ol-dillard-to-practice-squad-release-player|website=49ers.com|date=October 28, 2025|access-date=October 28, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Sign OL Brandon Parker to Practice Squad, Release OL Andre Dillard|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-ol-brandon-parker-to-practice-squad-release-ol-andre-dillard|website=49ers.com|date=October 30, 2025|access-date=October 31, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dillard grew up in Woodinville, WA., to Jennifer Bollinger and father, Mitch, who had also played football for Washington State Cougars as an offensive lineman from 1983 to 1986.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nwnews.com/index.php/sports/11865-whs-football-ex-falcon-dillard-loving-life-at-wsu|title=WHS FOOTBALL: EX-FALCON DILLARD LOVING LIFE AT WSU|author=Johnson|first=Derek|date=August 31, 2015|work=[[The Woodinville Weekly]]|access-date=May 3, 2018|archive-date=June 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601165629/http://nwnews.com/index.php/sports/11865-whs-football-ex-falcon-dillard-loving-life-at-wsu|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
At [[San Jose State University]], Chachere played at [[cornerback]] for the [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State Spartans]] from 2014 to 2017. After playing primarily on [[special teams]] in his first season, Chachere was a starter for his last three seasons. In 49 career games, Chachere had 122 total tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss for 14 yards (including a sack), three forced fumbles, seven interceptions for 169 yards, and 27 passes defended.<ref name="SJSU"/> In San Jose State's 27-16 victory over [[2015 Georgia State Panthers football team|Georgia State]] in the [[2015 Cure Bowl]], Chachere made an interception in the end zone in the final minute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sanjosest_ftp.sidearmsports.com/custompages/sports/m-footbl/stats/2015-2016/cure15.html|title=SJSUSpartans.com - Official Athletic Site of San José State University - Stats|website=sanjosest_ftp.sidearmsports.com}}</ref> Chachere graduated from San Jose State in May 2018 with a bachelor's degree in communication studies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sjsuspartans.com/news/2018/5/23/Congratulations_To_Our_2018_Graduates_.aspx|title=Congratulations To Our 2018 Graduates!|publisher=San Jose State University|work=SJSUSpartans.com|date=May 23, 2018|accessdate=August 26, 2020|archive-date=May 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514091940/https://sjsuspartans.com/news/2018/5/23/congratulations_to_our_2018_graduates_.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Andre Fitzgerald Jones''' (May 15, 1969 – June 22, 2011) was an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for one season with the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in 1992. He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]], and was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the seventh round of the [[1991 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1991 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1991/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He died in 2011 due to a [[Intracranial aneurysm|brain aneurysm]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2011/06/22/former-notre-dame-player-andre-jones-dies-at-42/|title=Former Notre Dame player Andre Jones dies at 42|website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=22 June 2011 |publisher=|access-date=November 19, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He had five children, including three sons: [[T. J. Jones|T. J.]], [[Malachi Jones (gridiron football)|Malachi]], and [[Jahmai Jones|Jahmai]].  T. J. is a [[wide receiver]], Malachi is a wide receiver for the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL), and Jahmai is an [[outfielder]] for the [[Detroit Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/notre-dame-football/post/_/id/817/t-j-malachi-jones-live-through-fathers-lessons |title=Jones brothers live through dad's lessons |author=Matt Fortuna |date=September 22, 2011 |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures |work=www.espn.com |accessdate=July 28, 2018}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ocregister.com/angels/draft-665254-pick-round.html Angels select Georgia HS OF Jahmai Jones with 2nd-round pick in draft]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-03 |title=Brewers Sign Jahmai Jones |url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2023/07/brewers-sign-jahmai-jones.html |access-date=2023-07-04 |website=MLB Trade Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Andre James''' (born May 2, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]], before signing as an [[undrafted free agent]] with [[Oakland Raiders]] in 2019. 

==Early life==
James grew up in [[South Jordan, Utah]], and attended [[Herriman High School]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Reed |first=Tashan |date=2021-11-30 |title=‘I feel like I’ve grown a lot’: Andre James is settling in to his role as the Raiders’ starting center |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2983909/2021/11/30/i-feel-like-ive-grown-a-lot-andre-james-is-settling-in-to-his-role-as-the-raiders-starting-center/ |access-date=2025-07-29 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre James' father refused to let cancer take the fight out of him to the end |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/andre-james-father-refused-to-let-cancer-take-the-fight-out-of-him-to-the-end |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=Las Vegas Raiders |language=en-US}}</ref> where he was a member of the football and track and field teams. He was named first-team All-State as a senior at offensive tackle. James was also a three time class 5A state champion in the shot put.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2015 |title=Andre James: Four-star OT from Utah signs NLI with UCLA |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2015/02/04/andre-james-four-star-ot-from-utah-signs-nli-with-ucla/ |access-date=November 17, 2020 |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]}}</ref> He was rated a four-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at UCLA over offers from Oregon, USC, Ohio State, Oklahoma and Utah.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Conway |first=Tyler |date=July 10, 2014 |title=Andre James to UCLA: Bruins Land 4-Star OT Prospect |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2121920-andre-james-to-ucla-bruins-land-4-star-ot-prospect |access-date=November 17, 2020 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref>

==College career==
James was a member of the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]], [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his true freshman season. He became a starter during his redshirt freshman season following an injury to [[Kolton Miller]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kamrani |first=Christopher |date=November 1, 2017 |title=An emotional Utah homecoming is on tap for UCLA tackle, Herriman grad Andre James |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2017/11/01/an-emotional-homecoming-is-on-tap-for-ucla-tackle-herriman-grad-andre-james/ |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=[[Salt Lake Tribune]]}}</ref> James started the final 32 games of his collegiate career, appearing in 35 games total.<ref name=declare/> As a redshirt junior, he made the decision to play in the Bruins' week seven game against Arizona and continue his consecutive games started streak despite his father dying of cancer earlier that week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2018 |title=Andre James starts for UCLA five days after father's passing |url=https://www.dailynews.com/andre-james-starts-for-ucla-five-days-after-fathers-passing |access-date=November 17, 2020 |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]}}</ref> James declared for the NFL Draft on December 18, 2018, forgoing his final season of NCAA eligibility.<ref name="declare">{{Cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Thuc Nhi |date=December 18, 2018 |title=UCLA LT Andre James declares for NFL draft |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2018/12/19/ucla-lt-andre-james-declares-for-nfl-draft/ |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]}}</ref>

James signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 3, 2019. He was reunited with UCLA offensive tackle [[Kolton Miller]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bair |first=Scott |date=May 3, 2019 |title=Raiders sign 10 undrafted free agents, these three can make roster |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/raiders/raiders-sign-10-undrafted-free-agents-these-three-can-make-roster |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=[[NBC Sports Bay Area]]}}</ref> He made his NFL debut on September 9, 2019, against the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bair |first=Scott |date=September 10, 2019 |title=Raiders snap count: Darren Waller moved all around, never left field |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/raiders-snap-count-darren-waller-175520065.html |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |archive-date=October 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021142616/https://sports.yahoo.com/raiders-snap-count-darren-waller-175520065.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his first career start at center in Week 9 in place of the injured [[Rodney Hudson]]. On March 11, 2024, James signed a three-year, $24 million contract extension with the Raiders.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Marcus |date=2024-03-11 |title=Silver Minings: Andre James re-signs before free agency |url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2024/3/11/24096972/raiders-news-andre-james-free-agency |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=Silver And Black Pride |publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref>

'''Andre Jordan Cisco''' (born March 23, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]], and was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Cisco grew up in [[Valley Stream, New York]]<ref name="h656">{{cite web | last=Toscano | first=Nora | title=See this NFL safety come back home to inspire Valley Stream's future football stars | website=Herald Community Newspapers | date=2024-06-21 | url=https://www.liherald.com/stories/andre-cisco-valley-stream-football-camp,208525 | access-date=2024-12-26}}</ref> and attended [[St. Anthony's High School (South Huntington, New York)|St. Anthony's High School]] in [[South Huntington, New York]], before transferring to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]], prior to his junior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Nate |date=November 28, 2019 |title=Is the NFL coming sooner than later for Andre Cisco? |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/2019/11/the-nfl-could-come-sooner-than-later-for-andre-cisco-he-has-planned-for-this-his-whole-life.html |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=syracuse}}</ref> He committed to [[Syracuse University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Stephen |date=December 9, 2017 |title=3-star DB Andre Cisco commits to Syracuse football |url=https://www.newyorkupstate.com/syracuse-sports/2017/12/andre_cisco_commits_defensive_back_syracuse_football_recruiting.html |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=New York Upstate}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Stephen |date=August 7, 2018 |title=Syracuse's Andre Cisco 'not your average freshman'; will he start? |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/2018/08/andre_cisco_safety_syracuse_football_starter.html |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=syracuse}}</ref> Cisco stated he had never played a single snap on varsity in high school and had no scholarship offers. Prior to his junior season, he visited the IMG Academy and was offered enrollment after meeting with coaches.

==College career==
As a freshman at Syracuse in 2018, Cisco started 11 of 13 games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=St. Croix |first=Josh |date=September 9, 2018 |title=Orange freshman Cisco isn't kidding around |url=https://www.nny360.com/sports/orange-freshman-cisco-isn-t-kidding-around/article_2430b7cc-a2f9-582c-b47c-98ca24199caa.html |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=NNY360}}</ref> He recorded 60 tackles and seven [[interceptions]], which was tied for most in the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Stephen |date=May 3, 2019 |title=SU's Cisco wants to match All-American stats with performance |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/2019/05/syracuse-footballs-andre-cisco-wants-to-match-all-american-stats-with-play.html |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=syracuse}}</ref> He was the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]'s Defensive Rookie of the Year and was a freshman [[All-American]]. He became the first true freshman in school history to earn All-American honors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Stephen |date=November 27, 2018 |title=SU's Andre Cisco named ACC Defensive Rookie of Year |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/2018/11/andre_cisco_syracuse_football_defensive_rookie_year.html |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=syracuse}}</ref> On September 26, 2020, Cisco sustained a "lower body injury" while warming up for a game at Georgia Tech. On October 12, 2020, Syracuse head coach [[Dino Babers]] announced that Cisco would miss the remainder of the season due to a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]].<ref name="forgo"/> Cisco started nine games his sophomore season, missing three due to injury, and had 65 tackles, five interceptions and a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Cisco 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andre-cisco-1/gamelog/2019 |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On October 13, 2020, Cisco officially announced he would forego his remaining college eligibility to enter the draft after tearing his ACL.<ref name="forgo">{{cite web |title=Sports Summary: Cisco declares for 2021 NFL draft |url=https://www.thenewshouse.com/sports/cisco-declares-for-2021-nfl-draft-after-season-ending-injury/ |access-date=January 27, 2025 |website=thenewshouse.com| date=October 15, 2020}}</ref> He was ranked as the sixth best safety prospect in the draft by [[Pro Football Focus]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2021 NFL Draft safety rankings |url=https://www.pff.com/news/draft-2021-nfl-draft-safety-rankings |access-date=January 27, 2025 |website=PFF.com |author=Michael Rebber |date=April 19, 2021}}</ref> NFL analyst [[Bucky Brooks]] ranked Cisco fourth among all safeties while Dane Brugler of the [[New York Times]] ranked him fifth among all safeties.<ref>{{cite web| title=Bucky Brooks' top five 2021 NFL Draft prospects by position 3.0|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bucky-brooks-top-five-2021-nfl-draft-prospects-by-position-3-0 |access-date=January 27, 2025 |website=NFL.com |author=Bucky Brooks| date=April 21, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Dane Brugler |date=March 25, 2021 |title=Top 10 safeties for 2021 NFL Draft: Richie Grant, Trevon Moehrig lead the way |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2473862/2021/03/25/top-10-safeties-for-2021-nfl-draft-richie-grant-trevon-moehrig-lead-the-way/ |access-date=January 27, 2025 |website=nytimes.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars ===
The [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] selected Cisco in the third round (65th overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]]. He was the fourth safety drafted in 2021 and was the highest safety drafted from Syracuse since [[Tebucky Jones]] and [[Donavin Darius]] in [[1998 NFL draft|1998]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=April 30, 2021 |title=No. 65 overall: Cisco is the selection |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/no-65-overall-cisco-is-the-selection |access-date=May 8, 2021 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> Analysts contributed Cisco's fall in the draft to his ACL injury during his last collegiate season. He was considered by analysts to be one of the biggest possible potential "steals" in the 2021 NFL draft. Jaguars' head coach Urban Meyer stated Cisco was one of his favorite players on the board, post draft.<ref name="battle"/>

|quote="You watch him when he’s healthy and it’s hard to say he’s not the best safety in the draft."<ref name="battle"/>

====2021====
{{see also|2021 Jacksonville Jaguars season}}
On June 11, 2021, the Jacksonville Jaguars signed Cisco to a four–year, [[United States dollar|$]]5.23 million [[contract]] that includes an initial [[signing bonus]] of $1.16 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Sam |date=June 10, 2021 |title=NFL Draft Pick Signings: 6/10/21 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/06/nfl-draft-pick-signings-6-10-21 |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Andre Cisco contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/_/id/72445/andre-cisco |access-date=January 8, 2025 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> 
Although he was still recovering from an ACL tear, the Jaguars chose not to place him on the [[Physically unable to perform|Active/ PUP list]] at the start of [[training camp]]. He instead remained listed as active and was able to compete against [[Andrew Wingard]], Daniel Thomas, [[Josh Jones (safety)|Josh Jones]], [[Jarrod Wilson]], [[Rudy Ford]] to be the starting strong safety under defensive coordinator [[Joe Cullen (American football)|Joe Cullen]] throughout training camp.<ref>{{cite web| title=Here's the Jags' unofficial depth chart for their third preseason game vs. the Cowboys| url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2021/08/26/heres-the-jags-unofficial-depth-chart-for-their-third-preseason-game-vs-the-cowboys/ |access-date=January 27, 2025| website=jaguarswire.usatoday.com| author=James Johnson| date=August 26, 2021}}</ref> Head coach Urban Meyer named Cisco as a backup safety to begin the regular season, behind starting safeties [[Rayshawn Jenkins]] and Andrew Wingard, as well as primary backup [[Daniel Thomas (safety)|Daniel Thomas]].<ref name="battle">{{cite web| title=Jaguars' 2021 Training Camp Position Battles To Watch: Safety Spot Opposite Rayshawn Jenkins| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jaguars/news/jaguars-2021-training-camp-position-battles-to-watch-safety-spot-opposite-rayshawn-jenkins|access-date=January 27, 2025| website=si.com| author=Kassidy Hill| date=July 26, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Jaguars depth chart 2021: Jacksonville's 53-man roster, projected starters as season approaches |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/jaguars-depth-chart-2021-jacksonvilles-53-man-roster-projected-starters-as-season-approaches/ |access-date=January 27, 2025| website=cbssports.com| author=Jeff Kerr| date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>
{{quote box
|align=right
|width=50%
|quote="Andre [Cisco], before his injury, was probably the top safety in the country. I think he had 13 interceptions in about roughly two years, and he fits all the boxes in terms of the size, the speed, the athleticism. So, we’re really excited about those two additions via the draft."<ref name="battle"/>
|source=–[[Joe Cullen (American football)|Joe Cullen]], Jaguars defensive coordinator 
}}

On September 12, 2021, Cisco made his professional regular season debut in the Jacksonville Jaguars' season-opener at the [[2021 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]], but was limited to one solo tackle during the 21–37 loss. On December 16, 2021, the Jacksonville Jaguars fired head coach Urban Meyer due to multiple controversies. Offensive coordinator [[Darrell Bevell]] was inserted as the interim head coach for the remaining four games of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=A Statement from Shad Khan|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/a-statement-from-shad-khan|website=Jaguars.com|access-date=December 16, 2021|archive-date=December 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216055506/https://www.jaguars.com/news/a-statement-from-shad-khan|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|author=Gardner, Steve|title= Urban Meyer fired as Jaguars coach 13 games into first NFL season amid controversies|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/jaguars/2021/12/15/urban-meyer-fired-jacksonville-jaguars-coach-first-year/8917440002/|date= December 16, 2021|access-date=December 16, 2021}}</ref> On December 20, 2021, interim head coach Darrell Bevell named Cisco the starting free safety for the last three games of the season after Rayshawn Jenkins was placed on [[injured reserve]] due to a broken ankle he injured the previous day during a 16–30 loss at the [[2021 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Jaguars S Rayshawn Jenkins will miss rest of season due to broken ankle| url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2021/12/20/22846926/jaguars-s-rayshawn-jenkins-will-miss-rest-of-season-due-to-broken-ankle |access-date=January 27, 2025 |website=BigCatCountry.com |date=December 20, 2021 |author=Demetrius Harvey}}</ref> On December 26, 2021, Cisco earned his first career start and recorded five combined tackles (two solo) and had one pass break up during a 21–26 loss at the [[2021 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. The following week, he collected a season-high six combined tackles (five solo) and one pass deflection as the Jaguars were routed by the [[2021 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] 10–50. He finished his [[rookie]] campaign in 2021 with a total of 26 combined tackles (19 solo), two pass deflections, and two forced fumbles while appearing in all 17 games with three starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Cisco 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CiscAn00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2022====
{{see also|2022 Jacksonville Jaguars season}}
During training camp, Cisco competed against Andrew Wingard to be the starting safety under defensive coordinator [[Mike Caldwell (linebacker)|Mike Caldwell]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Training Camp 2022: Position battles to watch for the Jacksonville Jaguars| url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2022/7/8/23198340/nfl-training-camp-2022-position-battles-to-watch-jacksonville-jaguars |access-date=January 27, 2025 |website=BigCatCountry.com |author=Ryan O'Bleniss| date=July 8, 2022}}</ref> Head coach [[Doug Pederson]] named Cisco the starting free safety to begin the season, alongside Rayshawn Jenkins.<ref>{{cite web| title=Jaguars Release Depth Chart for Week 1 of the 2022 season| url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-release-depth-chart-for-week-1-of-the-2022-season |access-date=January 27, 2025 |website=Jaguars.com| date=September 6, 2022}}</ref>
[[File:Andre Cisco 2022 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|200px|Cisco playing for the Jaguars in 2022]]
On September 18, 2022, Cisco made six combined tackles (four solo), broke up a pass, and made his first career interception off a pass by [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] intended for [[Parris Campbell]] during a 24–0 victory against the [[2022 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. On October 2, 2022, Cisco recorded four combined tackles (three solo), a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Jalen Hurts]] to [[Zach Pascal]], returning it 59–yards for his first career touchdown during a 29–21 loss at the [[2022 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Philadelphia Eagles - October 2nd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210020phi.htm |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 6, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles (six solo) as the Jaguars lost 27–34 at the [[2022 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. He was sidelined for two games (Weeks 13–14) after injuring his shoulder. On December 22, 2022, he made three combined tackles (one solo) and had his first career sack on [[Zach Wilson]] during a 19–3 victory at the [[2022 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. He finished his sophomore season with a total of 73 combined tackles (49 solo), ten pass deflections, three interceptions, and one sack while starting all 15 games he appeared in.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Cisco 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CiscAn00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=February 25, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Jacksonville Jaguars finished first in the [[AFC South]] with a 9–8 record to clinch a playoff berth. On January 14, 2022, Cisco started in his first career playoff game and recorded four solo tackles and broke up a pass during a 31–30 victory against the [[2022 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]] in the AFC Wildcard Game. The following week, he made four combined tackles (three solo) as the Jaguars were eliminated from the playoffs after losing 20–27 at the [[2022 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] in the Divisional Round.

====2023====
{{see also|2023 Jacksonville Jaguars season}}
He returned as the starting free safety in 2023, along with strong safety Rayshawn Jenkins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars release official 2023 depth chart ahead of Week 1 opener| url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/lists/jaguars-depth-chart-2023-official-week-1/ |access-date=January 28, 2025 |website=jaguarswire.usatoday.com |author=Adam Stites| date=September 5, 2023}}</ref> On September 10, 2023, he started in the Jacksonville Jaguars' season-opener at the [[2023 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] and collected a season-high ten combined tackles (seven solo) in their 31–21 victory. The following week, he had two combined tackles (one solo), a season-high two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Patrick Mahomes]] intended for [[Justin Watson (wide receiver)|Justin Watson]] during a 17–9 loss. He was inactive during a Week 8 victory at the [[2023 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] after injuring his hamstring.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars' Andre Cisco Named to ESPN's All-Under 24 List| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jaguars/news/jaguars-andre-cisco-named-to-espns-all-under-24-list |access-date=January 28, 2025 |website=syracuse.com| date=November 28, 2023| author=John Shipley}}</ref> In Week 14, he recorded three solo tackles before exiting in the third quarter of a 27–31 loss at the [[2023 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Andre Cisco leaves Jaguars game with injury (Syracuse, CNY in NFL Week 14)| url=https://www.syracuse.com/sports/2023/12/andre-cisco-leaves-jaguars-game-with-injury-syracuse-cny-in-nfl-week-14.html |access-date=January 28, 2025 |website=syracuse.com| date=December 11, 2023| author=Geoff Herbert}}</ref> The following week, Cisco remained inactive due to his injury as the Jaguars lost 7–23 against the [[2023 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]]. He finished the [[2023 NFL season]] with a total of 62 combined tackles (42 solo), five pass deflections, four interceptions, and was credited with half a sack in 15 games and 15 starts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pro-Football-Reference: Andre Cisco stats (2023)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CiscAn00.htm |access-date=January 28, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

'''Andre Baccellia''' (born January 7, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]] and was originally signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in {{NFL Year|2020}}. He later played for the [[New England Patriots]] and [[Arizona Cardinals]].

==Early life==
Baccellia was born on January 7, 1997, in [[Thousand Oaks, California]]. He attended high school there for [[Westlake High School (California)|Westlake]], playing [[American football|football]] and [[Track and field|track]]. As a junior in high school, Baccellia caught 46 passes for 954 yards and 11 [[touchdowns]], helping his team achieve an 8–3 record. As a senior, he missed time due to injury but still managed to gain 392 yards on 18 catches, scoring 5 touchdowns. In track, he finished third place in the 100 meter race at the Ventura County Championships.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://gohuskies.com/sports/football/roster/andre-baccellia/9466|title=Andre Baccellia|website=Washington Huskies}}</ref> He was ranked the 78th best recruit in California and the 104th receiver overall.

==College career==
He was given a scholarship to play for [[University of Washington]]. He spent his true freshman year as a redshirt, and did not play for their [[Washington Huskies football|Huskies football team]]. In his first game the following year, Baccellia recorded two catches for 40 yards and one touchdown in the season opener against [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers]]. He made his first career start later that year, versus [[Portland State Vikings football|Portland State]]. He finished the season with 7 catches for 98 yards and one touchdown.<ref name="auto"/>

He played in just seven games as a sophomore, starting four. Baccellia finished the year with 16 catches for 187 yards. He also threw a 52-yard pass against [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]] in the [[Fiesta Bowl]]. He played in all 14 games the following year, starting five. He became more involved on offense as a junior in 2018, making 55 catches for 584 yards. As a senior, Baccellia played in all but one game, and recorded 29 receptions for 314 yards and four touchdowns.<ref name="auto"/>

he finished the year with two receptions for eight yards across five games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Root |first=Jess |title=Arizona Cardinals make roster moves in Week 16 |url=https://cardswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2025/12/16/arizona-cardinals-make-roster-moves-in-week-16/87799389007/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=Cardinals Wire |language=en-US}}</ref>

Baccellia was released by the Cardinals on May 7, 2026, following a failed physical.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Cardinals sign three draft picks, cut WR Andre Baccellia |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/cardinals-sign-three-draft-picks-cut-wr-andre-baccellia |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=NBCSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Andre Anthony''' (born November 21, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]]. He is currently the new head coach at [[Alfred Bonnabel High School|Bonnabel High School]] in Kenner, Louisiana.

==College career==
Anthony redshirted his first year at [[Louisiana State University]] due to issues with his academic transcripts. In 2017, he was sidelined by a Lisfranc injury. He returned in 2018, appearing in 13 games with three starts, recording 14 tackles and half a sack. The following season, he contributed to LSU's national championship run, playing in nine games, starting twice, and finishing with nine tackles and one sack.<ref name="p222">{{cite web | title=Anthony becomes 10th player drafted from LSU with seventh-round selection by Tampa Bay | website=Tiger Rag | date=2022-04-30 | url=https://www.tigerrag.com/anthony-becomes-10th-player-drafted-from-lsu-with-seventh-round-selection-by-tampa-bay/ | access-date=2024-12-26}}</ref> In 2020, Anthony started eight games, leading the team with 5.5 sacks and recording 24 total tackles. In the 2021 season, he suffered a knee injury, which ended his final season early.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reuter |first=Chad |last2=Zierlein |first2=Lance |title=Andre Anthony Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/andre-anthony/3200414e-5409-2384-d11e-26be2a809543 |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Andre''' "'''Dre'''" '''Miller''' (born April 18, 1998) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Maine Black Bears football|Maine]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lazarczyk |first=Travis  |date=July 30, 2022 |title=Andre Miller looking to defy the odds once again |work=Press Herald |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2022/07/30/andre-miller-looking-to-defy-the-odds-once-again/ |access-date=July 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mahoney |first=Larry |date=February 1, 2023 |title=Andre Miller trains in Bangor to rejoin the New York Giants next season |work=Bangor Daily News |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2023/02/01/sports/professional-sports/andre-miller-trains-bangor-new-york-giants-joam40zk0w/ |access-date=July 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=May 1, 2022 |title=Andre Miller signs with New York Giants as free agent |language=en |work=University of Maine Athletics |url=https://goblackbears.com/news/2022/5/1/football-andre-miller-signs-with-new-york-giants-as-free-agent.aspx |access-date=July 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=October 26, 2022 |title=New York Giants sign former UMaine receiver Andre Miller to practice squad |work=Bangor Daily News |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2022/10/25/sports/professional-sports/new-york-giants-sign-umaine-andre-miller/ |access-date=July 23, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
===Husson===
Andre Miller played [[wide receiver]] at [[Husson Eagles football|Husson]] for his freshman season. In 2016, he played in 10 games with 13 receptions, 152 yards, and 1 touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Miller – 2016 – Football |url=https://hussoneagles.com/sports/football/roster/andre-miller/1861 |access-date=July 23, 2023 |website=Husson University |language=en}}</ref>

===Maine===
In 2018, Miller appeared in 9 games and had 5 receptions with 109 yards, and 1 touchdown. During Maine's NCAA Semifinal game at Eastern Washington Miller had a career-highs in receptions 9 and receiving yards 129 with his first career touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldberg |first=Rob |date=December 15, 2018 |title=Eastern Washington Beats Maine, Advances to FCS Title Game vs. North Dakota St. |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2810962-eastern-washington-beats-maine-advances-to-fcs-title-game-vs-north-dakota-st |access-date=July 23, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>

In 2019, Miller appeared in 11 games and had 28 receptions with 528 yards, and 4 touchdowns. Miller set an all-time record with a 90-yard touchdown reception.

In 2021, Miller appeared in 9 games and had 39 receptions with 684 yards, and 6 touchdowns. He was named to the All-CAA First Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Miller – Football |url=https://goblackbears.com/sports/football/roster/andre-miller/7809 |access-date=July 23, 2023 |website=University of Maine Athletics |language=en}}</ref>
